items.body: Review by Aussie-Byrd-Brother — 2025 brought the exciting news that Swedish female-fronted prog band Paatos had not only regrouped, but were ready to deliver a brand new studio work. `Timeloss', their debut from 2002, was a minor modern prog classic, effortlessly blending gloomy rock, weary jazz, hypnotic ambience and even glitching trip-hop and electronica. The departure of early guitarist Reine Fiske (finding success with alt-rockers Dungen) only slightly affected their sound, with the group retaining the sullen atmospheres but adopting more of an alternative rock/intelligent pop approach, even attracting to attention of modern prog notable Steven Wilson enough to work on their second album `Kallocain'.Thirteen years on from their last work, the same line-up since 2011's `Breathing' now offers `Ligament', and it shows the band continuing to experiment and break new ground, whilst also retaining all the subtle dynamics, melancholic moods, bursts of power and air of mystery that permeated all their previous works. Murky cinematic rock, wilting ballads, eerie distortions and freeform jams all blur together, and it even boasts a guest appearance from Mikael Akerfeldt of progressive-minded metal act Opeth.Launching to a cavalcade of Huxflux Nettermalm's breakneck drumming, opener `Chemical Escape' hits the ground running, all frantic energy and rattling bluster with a muscular chorus. Ulf Ivarsson's gorgeously murmuring, grooving bass (front and center the entire album) and Peter Nylander's shimmering guitars with grinding King Crimson-like reaching strains get mangled together, and while Petronella Nettermalm sighs and breathily coos "I'll be perfectly alright", the slinking and skittering electronic/drum-n-bass breakdown and stark violin scratches in the climax suggest overwise.The relentless `Beyond the Forest' is too up-tempo to be a traditional ballad, rather it's a darkly sultry duet between Petronella and Opeth's Mikael Akerfeldt that's full of longing...and a definite hint of danger. Wrapping around their voices is creaking cello and grand Mellotron rises, and the dark ambient outro ends on a very ambiguous note - is the piece about two lovers passionately pining for each-other, or is one of them trying to escape the dangerously obsessed other? You be the judge.Reflective and evocative ballad `I Deny' tiptoes with crystalline piano and ringing guitars that glisten with pristine beauty. Short but not even slightly sweet, the two-minute title-track is a breakneck runaway tantrum of noise, Petronella's voice a distorted snarl writhing around barb-wire guitars, and `Post War Liminal' is a lurching, stop-start staccato drone that wouldn't have sounded out of place on a Bass Communion album.Opening to weeping Mellotron veils, `I'm Letting Go' is a powerful yet reflective indie pop-rocker that soars with hope thanks to Petronella's defiant and rousing vocal. While her spectral voice looms and soars around `Who Am I', it's hard to relax with how `off' in parts the piece sounds, crumbling into the embers of a jazz-fusion improvisation, all scratching and scraping distortion, abrasive effects, ghostly and discordant piano and grumbling guitar trembles before its equally uneasy ambient close.`November' is a reflective lament around the gentlest of jazz patterings and lowly cavernous reverberations. But siren calls and angelic harmonies are quickly ripped to shreds with the violent `Last Ones of Our Kind', a raging political attack that ripples with danger and breathless tension. Patronella warns there's "no redemption to the found", and while offering one of the more overtly obvious and striking chorus moments of the disc, the band whips up a suitably stormy noise with multiple improvised passages of wavering keyboard swirls, crushing drums and blistering guitar salvos, sounding not unlike moments of Steven Wilson's solo works.Lurking closer `Svart' presses down heavy on the listener and refuses to remove its boot, a mucky gothic dirge that, despite the most minuscule glimpses of hope and respite, grumbles with a Magma/Zuehl-like oppression with its pounding percussion and dingy gulping bass. What, you thought with lyrics like the "Nothing will remain, nothing with live..." that the band would end on smiles and sunshine?!With this latest work, the band achieves a near-perfect balance of new directions and expected intense atmospheres that are still instantly recognisable as Paatos, but they are now not afraid to unsettle or move away from the more melodic, tune-based material of several of their last few releases. Petronella's voice has never been so powerful, and the instrumental interplay from the fellas has never moved so seamlessly from complex to subtle. It means `Ligament' is their darkest, most daring and experimental release yet, and certainly their strongest and most exciting effort since their debut.Welcome back, Paatos - four stars.(please note - `Port War Liminal' and `November' seem to be sadly absent from the LP release)
items._genre: crossover prog / art rock / dark ambient / electronic
items._cn_summary: 瑞典乐队Paatos暌违十三年推出新作《Ligament》，延续其阴郁电影化的氛围基调，同时拓展声音边界。专辑将黯淡摇滚、另类流行与自由即兴段落相互融合，融入电子碎拍、弦乐采样、曼陀林琴织体与黑暗环境声效。女主唱Petronella Nettermalm的叹息式低语与变形嘶吼交替呈现，贝斯始终居于混音核心位置，吉他线条闪烁而不失粗粝张力。Opeth主唱Mikael Akerfeldt客串的曲目以对唱形式铺陈暧昧叙事，结尾坠入深沉环境氛围。整体编曲在爆发力段落与静谧冥想间不断切换，兼具结构感与即兴自由，体现出乐队对动态对比与情绪层次的持续探索。

items._cn_summary: 这张限量27份的收藏版盒装由Karl Bösmann与Wataru Kasahara合作呈现，跨越三张黑胶与两张CD-R，将电子、噪音、抽象与当代古典拼贴为一体。Bösmann的作品如《Mindfucker》《Traffic Brain》以及长达42段的《A Drone Called Monster 1-42》运用噪音墙与持续音手法，CD-R《Fuckminder》中标题如《I Hate My Dentist》《Found Myself Dead》透露出黑色幽默与即兴拼贴的倾向。Kasahara的钢琴独奏作品12段则提供截然不同的声学维度，与Bösmann的电子暴力形成对照。Stabat Mors的《Fraktale》使用分形结构构建循环序列，介于古典结构与后现代解构之间。整体走地下厂牌路线，使用回收唱碟盒作为包装，强调每一份的独一无二性，是面向极端收藏者的小众实验合集。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由RRRecords发行的实验合辑，邀请500位艺术家各自贡献一段锁槽音轨（lock-groove），收录在多张LP上。曲目全部以Untitled命名，涵盖另类摇滚、噪音、口语、抽象、嗡鸣、硬核、工业及实验等多种边缘风格，参与者包括Otomo Yoshihide、池田亮司、Zoviet France、Bruce Gilbert、Felix Kubin等知名实验音乐人。由于每段音轨被锁定在无限循环的凹槽中，作品本质上是将唱片媒介本身转化为声音雕塑，强调声音的物质性与重复性。合辑作为一场集体行为艺术，体现了九十年代末地下实验音乐场景对格式与媒介边界的探索。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — From its humble origins as Wiccan Rede to its earliest albums as NEGURA BUNGET, this Romanian bandelegantly began weaving in an increasingly strong aspect of progressive rock with each releaseslowly emerging as something more complex than what preceded. Two albums in and NEGURA BUNGET was amajor world class powerhouse of exquisitely designed atmospheric Pagan metal that took fulladvantage of the progressive metal lexicon and with N CRUGU BRADULUI, the band's third full-lengthrelease, the band that now consisted of the original duo drummer Negru and guitarist / vocalist /keyboardist Hupogrammos Disciple's along with guitarist Cristian Popescu "Sol Faur" and guestbassist Ursu went for the progressive jugular.Wild claims state that the title translates into something exotic such as "Through The Deepness OfThe Fir Tree Heights," which is parroted across the internet but it seems that the album's title NCRUGU BRADULU simply translates as "Around The Fir Tree." The album debuted the band's fullestprogressive potentials which features an epic concept of the natural cycle of the universe andbroken down into four lengthy tracks that each represents one of the four seasons with tracksranging between 12 and 15 minutes in length. The album ramps up the band's flawless atmosphericfusion of aggressive black metal along with synthesized arrangements and eerie ambient effects.Likewise the band introduced more aspects of its native Romanian folk music with the timeless soundsof Transylvania seeping in.With four chapters simply titled "I" through "IV," N CRUGU BRADULUI offers haunting atmosphericbuildup to ratchet up the mystique before erupting into a frenzy of black metal bombast and in theprocess evokes the dreamy atmospheric ambience of Burzum with the high octane energetic drive ofDarkthrone only fueled with the folk flavors of its homeland. "I" takes opens elegantly with a post-rock inspired introduction that slowly ratchets up the tension to a wonderful display of exquisitemusicianship in cahoots with well crafted compositions that keep your attention focused and thennever let you off the hook for the album's near 54 minute journey. The album elegantly blends thePagan mystique of Romanian antiquity while capturing the dark essence of Transylvania's #1 export,the Dracula mythos despite that not being the subject.While the following "OM" gets touted as the band's masterpiece of its career and for great reason asit takes what was presented on N CRUGU BRADULUI to even greater levels of ingenuity andexperimentation, for my tastes i find this predecessor to be on equal standing of its more laudedcounterpart. This album is flawless in execution and showcases the band's first perfecting balancebetween the atmospheric cryptic nature of the album's thematic structuring and magnificently matureblack metal that seamlessly fuses in the Romanian folk musical touches. The band had matured in everpossible way and although "OM" may be a tad more diverse with more excursions into pure folkritualistic effects, N CRUGU BRADULUI evokes the true majesty of Romanian black metal at its toptier level and every bit as enthralling as its followup. Just as much as a classic.
items._genre: pagan black metal / progressive metal / Romanian folk / atmospheric metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是罗马尼亚乐队NEGURA BUNGET的第三张全长作品，以四季循环为概念分为四首长篇曲目，每首时长十二至十五分钟。乐队将黑色金属的侵略性、前卫金属的复杂结构与罗马尼亚特兰西瓦尼亚地区的民俗音乐融合，合成器编排与阴森氛围音效贯穿始终，营造出浓郁的异教神秘感。前摇滚式的引子缓慢蓄积张力，随后爆发为黑金属狂潮。专辑探讨宇宙自然循环与罗马尼亚古老神秘主义，并非直接取材于吸血鬼传说，但在氛围上捕捉到特兰西瓦尼亚的黑暗精髓。乐评认为这张作品在主题结构与黑金属成熟度之间达成了首次完美平衡，融合民俗音乐的手法无痕而精妙，与乐队后续名作'OM'相比各有千秋。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Poly-Math are a British instrumental act formed in 2013 by guitarist Tim Walters who was originally drummer of post-rock band Monsters Build Mean Robots. He wanted to focus on guitar and instrumental music and was soon joined by bassist Joe Branton and drummer Chris Woollison. Shortly after the release of their 2018 album, 'House Of Wisdom | We Are The Devil' they were joined by American multi-instrumentalist Josh Geesner, who had relocated to the UK, and although they moved to a quintet for a short while with saxophonist Chris Olsen joining the ranks they are once again operating as a quartet. Musically this is all over the place with an incredibly diverse set of influences ranging from early classic prog, Ethio-jazz, post-rock, math rock, African tribal rhythms and so much more. There is a great deal going on at all times with hugely complex and complicated arrangements and massive note density, which means the listener needs to pay close attention to what is taking place or running the very real risk of missing out. Everyone involved is a master musician, yet there is little in the way of egos or hogging the limelight as all have a hugely important part to play in the overall sound as the percussion can be working in one direction which is totally at odds with the guitar while the bass is off on its own melody and the keyboards are taking another route, yet when they combine, it all makes sense. They will converge at a point; take a split second to remind each other they are all in the same band and then they are off again!While math rock is the main style, they bring in a great deal more, and Woollison is a true percussionist, not just a drummer wanting to expand his resume, which adds greatly to the overall impact.Truly progressive, this is a fascinating album from beginning to end.
items._genre: post-rock / math rock / experimental progressive / world fusion
items._cn_summary: POLY-MATH 是英国器乐乐队，由原鼓手 Tim Walters 转型吉他手后创立，2026 年发表专辑《Something Deeply Hidden》。乐队风格跨度极大，融合经典前卫摇滚、埃塞俄比亚爵士、后摇、数学摇滚以及非洲部落节奏等多重元素。编曲极度复杂，音符密度极高，要求听众全神贯注才能捕捉层次。吉他、贝斯、键盘与打击乐各自分头行进，互不相让，却能在特定瞬间汇合，让人惊叹于乐队成员的高超技术与默契。鼓手 Woollison 作为真正的打击乐手而非普通鼓手，为整体增添了丰富的节奏纹理。整张专辑从前到后保持高度的音乐性与探索性，是一张不妥协的前卫器乐作品。

items.body: Une Vraie Gothique (translated as A True Goth) is a French duo formed by Ulrika and Ferdinand Legendre. “R.D.V. Au Cimetière” is their debut album, and it immediately caught the attention of Manic Depression Records. The project’s name may sound unmistakably Gothic, but the musical influences stem from a much broader palette. This is primarily an Electro album, blending elements of Electro-Wave, EBM, Techno, and a subtle Gothic atmosphere into a highly danceable whole. The lyrics possess a poetic quality, occasionally veering into the humorous and sometimes even the provocative. The songs are performed in French by the male vocalist and in German by the female vocalist. The interplay between these two voices is one of the album’s greatest strengths, often creating the impression of an ongoing dialogue. The overall production occasionally reminds me of Grausame Töchter, albeit with far less emphasis on sexuality and provocation. Personally, I am most drawn to the more powerful tracks driven by a strong EBM bassline, but nearly every song offers something worthwhile. For me, “R.D.V. Au Cimetière” is an exciting and refreshing debut. Une Vraie Gothique is undoubtedly a band that deserves to be discovered, and they clearly possess the talent and originality needed to reach a much wider audience in the future. (Rating:8½). Listen to “Metz Noire”: https://manicdepressionrecords.bandcamp.com/track/metz-noire
items._cn_summary: 法国双人组合Une Vraie Gothique的首张专辑将Electro-Wave、EBM、Techno与哥特氛围融合，打造出高度适于舞池的电子声响。男女声部分别以法语和德语演绎，诗歌化的歌词偶尔流露出幽默与挑衅意味，两种语言的交织形成持续的对话感，成为专辑最突出的亮点。制作层面整体令人联想到Grausame Töchter，但减少了情色与挑衅元素，更侧重节奏与低音的驱动力。评论者特别偏爱EBM贝斯线主导的强劲曲目，认为几乎每首歌都提供了值得一听的内容。作为一张法语区出品的电子作品，其跨语言演唱与多元素整合的尝试，展现了独立厂牌背景下新人组合的原创潜力。

items.body: Boy Harsher returns with “Jeans,” their first new original song under the Boy Harsher banner since the cinematic 2022 stretch that brought The Runner and “Burn It Down” from the Halloween Ends soundtrack into their dance-noir universe. Arriving after the announcement of The Heartbreak Tour, the new track feels less like a simple comeback than a bold re-entry: a stonewashed post-punk fever dream about escape, ambition, image, and the uneasy moment when the fantasy of freedom gets refitted into a commodity. Musically, “Jeans” may be Boy Harsher’s most openly post-punk-sounding track yet. More guitar-forward than anything in their catalog, and with a bubbling synth beat, it finds Gus Muller riding a bouncy guitar riff that sounds as if it were pilfered from his foray into Safe Mind. It is a bold breath of fresh air for the duo, cutting through their usual synth-driven machinery with a wiry melodic lift. Threaded beneath it is a steel-slide guitar, giving the song the perfect western cowboy twang to match the line-dancing imagery in the video. The juxtaposition works because Jae Matthews knows exactly how to occupy the space around it. Her vocal here is sultry, cool, and lightly scuffed at the edges, less an incantation from a dark room than a sideways glance from the passenger seat. Against the guitar’s buoyant post-punk snap, “Jeans” takes on an almost Pretenders-like shape: sleek, restless, and deceptively direct, with noir atmosphere refracted through something closer to a new wave song’s 80s pop pulse. In a statement accompanying the release, Matthews says: “‘Jeans’ came from two distinct experiences between Gus and I. I was living in a ‘small town,’ trying to understand my life and attempting to find freedom from the pressure of being ‘anyone.’ Meanwhile, Gus was chasing his aspirations in the Big Apple. We were both seeking our dreams in polar ways … and in this cheeky way, ‘Jeans’ speaks on that quest through our commodification of a dream.” The band also described the video’s concept on Instagram: “We wanted to make our own Robert Palmer, “Addicted to Love.” We wanted to line dance in latex. Hot hands and cattle prods. We wanted to try to encapsulate that small-town feeling in an inaccessible apple.” Filmed by Owen Smith-Clark and edited by Chris Campion, the Boy Harsher-directed video places a pink-haired The 7th Girl, Ella, in a large, mostly empty room with fluorescent lights, tall windows, and pale walls. A group of dancers in black latex enters and performs line-dance choreography around her. Matthews sings in the room while Muller plays guitar, and both appear on old television monitors throughout the clip. The video cuts between close-ups of boots, gloves, latex, denim, faces, and the dancers’ formations. Some shots show the performers carrying cattle-prod-like props; others focus on the pink-haired woman as she watches the group, moves with them, and appears against a warm, western-colored backdrop. The clip keeps returning to the monitors, where close-ups of eyes and performance footage flicker inside the frame. A small town can feel like a sealed room; yet ambition can feel like another kind of enclosure. Freedom looks different from far away, especially when someone has already figured out how to turn longing into a look. Whether “Jeans” is the first flare from a larger body of work or simply the opening signal of Boy Harsher’s next phase, it arrives with the uneasy precision of a transmission from somewhere familiar and wonderfully strange. Watch the video for “Jeans” below: “Jeans” lands as Boy Harsher prepares for The Heartbreak Tour, their first extensive North American headlining run since the 2022 tour cycle around The Runner, when select dates paired the live show with screenings of the duo’s short horror film. They have continued to surface through select shows, festival appearances, remix work, soundtrack projects, and adjacent solo endeavors, but the center of gravity has shifted away from the usual album-tour pattern and toward film, scoring, and world-building. Matthews and Muller, who met in Savannah while studying film, first released Lesser Man as a small-run cassette before the EP became an underground hit. They followed with Yr Body Is Nothing in 2016 and Careful in 2019, sharpening their cold, body-moving electronics into something increasingly cinematic. That impulse became explicit with The Runner, the duo’s 2022 short horror film and accompanying soundtrack, written, produced, and directed by Matthews and Muller. The project blurred album, score, and visual world-building, pairing the duo’s darker instrumentals with guest turns from Mariana Saldaña of BOAN on “Machina” and Cooper B. Handy, aka Lucy, on “Autonomy.” The Machina thread continued in 2024 with the Machina EP, which expanded the track with alternate versions and remixes. Boy Harsher also kept a steady presence through remix work, including their 2024 rework of Pet Shop Boys’ “New London Boy,” a pairing that made sense: two duos fascinated by desire, distance, pop architecture, and the strange glamour of the city after dark. Matthews, meanwhile, has been building a parallel life in film and solo-adjacent work. She wrote My Animal, the Jacqueline Castel-directed horror romance starring Bobbi Salvör Menuez and Amandla Stenberg, which premiered at the 2023 Sundance Film Festival. This year, she stepped out under her own name with a cover of Buzz Kull’s “Man On The Beat,” released digitally March 20 and issued as a limited 12-inch through Heartworm Press on April 17. The physical edition, released as Heartworm #140 in an edition of 500, pairs Matthews’ version with a Spike Hellis remix on the B-side. Muller has continued to deepen his own work as a composer and producer. His score for My Animal, released by Sacred Bones, marked his debut feature film score and was written and recorded at his home studio in Northampton using hardware and analog synthesizers. He has also pursued Safe Mind, his collaborative project with Cooper B. Handy. The duo’s debut album, Cutting the Stone, arrived in 2025 through Nude Club, extending the chemistry first heard when Handy appeared on Boy Harsher’s The Runner soundtrack. The biggest new chapter, however, is The Lonely Woman, Boy Harsher’s first feature film as directors. Written and directed by Matthews and Muller, the rural New England horror-thriller stars Chloë Sevigny, FKA twigs, Sturgill Simpson, Will Oldham, and Jake Weary, with Boy Harsher also providing the score. The Heartbreak Tour began with a June 26 appearance at 1015 Folsom in San Francisco before properly kicking into gear Sept. 25 at Basilica Hudson in Hudson, New York. From there, Boy Harsher will move through Boston, Montreal, Toronto, Detroit, Chicago, Minneapolis, Denver, Portland, Seattle, Vancouver, Oakland, Los Angeles, Del Mar, Las Vegas, Phoenix, Fort Worth, New Orleans, Atlanta, Asheville, Washington, D.C., Philadelphia, and Queens, where the tour wraps Nov. 5 at Knockdown Center. The routing includes two-night stands at Chicago’s Metro, Portland’s Revolution Hall, and Seattle’s The Showbox, along with an Oct. 24 appearance at Sick New World – DFW in Fort Worth. Support on select dates includes Choir Boy, Evanora Unlimited, True Blue, and Kassie Krut. The centerpiece of the fall trek lands on Halloween night, when Boy Harsher headline Making Time Pure Halloween at Franklin Music Hall in Philadelphia. The Oct. 31 All Hallows’ Eve event also features Model/Actriz live, Conducta, Marie Davidson on DJ duty, Kassie Krut live, and Dave P., plus a futuristic visual experience from Klip Collective. items._cn_summary: Boy Harsher 携新单曲《Jeans》回归，这是乐队自2022年电影化时期以来的首支新作。歌曲在合成器基底之上引入更多吉他元素，bouncy吉他riff搭配钢滑棒吉他，营造出西部牛仔式的twang质感，与主唱Jae Matthews略带沙哑的冷调人声形成呼应。歌词探讨小镇生活压力与都市追梦之间的矛盾，以及梦想如何被商品化这一主题。音乐录影带由乐队自导，致敬Robert Palmer的视觉风格，粉发女子在荧光灯下的空旷房间中与乳胶装舞者展开line-dance编舞，通过牛仔、电击棒等意象强化商品的荒诞感。整体而言，这是一首将暗潮氛围折射入新波80年代流行脉动的作品，比以往更直接、更具旋律张力。

items.body:
5 Gate Temple's anomalous wildcard St Agnis yields another crooked gem under the Victoria Mingot alias - all enchantingly casual, even barely-there, lowercase strums and murmurs, like diaries of broken sleep FFO Joane Robertson, Loren Connors, Graham Lambkin.

‘God Spill’ takes things to their quietest, most ruminative depths; the dozen pieces are mostly instrumental, defined by plaintive melodic structuring for acoustic guitar on what sounds like dictaphone recordings that imbue everything with an eerie intimacy. However, there are vocals, and they’re pretty special when they do appear, like a flickering filament in the aether of ‘i saw the sign’, recalling Mary Maddox off Mike Ratledge’s ‘Riddles of the Sphinx’, floating, Virginia Astley-like, on the frayed Lambkin-esque strum of ‘in plentitude of the harvest’, or more textural in the mournful raga meditation ‘om dhyana’.

This exquisitely discreet balance of unshowy yet transfixing instrumental economy makes other works such as ‘before you fly’ stand out even more for its shimmering blend of Joanne Robertson and Loren Connors-like substance, and the whole record fully reveals itself with repeat listens.

Special stuff.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以极度克制的方式呈现十二首短曲，主要以原声吉他为载体，采用类似口述录音机的低保真录音质感，营造出一种破碎睡眠般的亲密氛围。多数曲目为纯器乐，旋律哀婉且结构极简，间或出现的人声如同漂浮在空气中的闪烁细丝，空灵而脆弱，与背景中的吉他编织融为一体。专辑中有一首带有挽歌气质的市场冥想曲，以及一些接近兰姆金式拨弦的织体片段。整体在'不炫耀但令人着迷'的器乐经济性之间取得了精妙平衡，部分曲目如'before you fly'则展现出更明显的闪烁质感，需要反复聆听才能完全展开。评论将其与乔安·罗伯逊、洛伦·康纳斯和格雷厄姆·兰姆金的风格并列，强调其私密与不规则的美学特质。

items.body:
R&B outsider Zsela joins forces with inc. no world's Daniel Aged and film composer Taul Katz on '4 Dreams', a billowing ambient-neoclassical hallucination that'll tickle fans of Mary Lattimore, Malibu, Nala Sinephro, Gigi Masin.

If you only know Zsela thanks to her dramatic 2024 debut album 'Big For You', the mostly beatless, fully reflective '4 Dreams' might come as a surprise. But look a little further back in her catalogue and things will fall into place; remember 'Angels Pharmacy' and Remembrance' from Actress's 'Karma & Desire'? That was Zsela on vocals, so she's got priors. '4 Dreams' started life as the soundtrack to 'Seven Heavenly Senses', an art exhibition from last year at Paris's Hôtel de la Marine, but has since taken on a life of its own. Zsela's breaths are stretched and sculpted into warm, washing biomechanical pads on the opening dream, left to weather tinny arpeggiated FM synths and muggy bass drones. So far, so predictable. But Zsela muddles proceedings with her confident delivery, layering her voice into jazzy, R&B inflected key changes that keep you guessing. Imagine an astral plane answer to Dawn Richard's ambient-inflected pop and you'll have some idea of where this is headed.

Then 'Dream 2' takes an unexpected diversion, the vocals replaced by swirling harp flourishes and the kind of floating synth stabs that draw a core logic from classic Ambient - Harold Budd, Laraaji et al - then adding extra colors just where necessary. And on 'Dream 3', faint, almost folk-y strings enter the frame, calling out from beyond the horizon, almost blotted out by a synth part that's in the thrall of Gigi Masin's legendary 'Clouds' - the track that ended up being repurposed by Björk on 'It's In Our Hands'. Zsela, Katz and Aged keep that momentum for the final track, too, letting cinematic strings echo around subtle synths and vanishing rhythms, hitting those hypnagogic, tranquil notes that so much contemporary ambient music seems to avoid. 'Cause at its heart, '4 Dreams' is deeper than that, a record that's entrenched in jazz, soul and classical minimalism rather than throwaway numbing music, of the contemporary varierty.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以氛围为底色、融合新古典与R&B人声的四首组曲，最初为巴黎海军酒店的艺术展览而创作，后独立发展成完整作品。Zsela的人声被拉伸塑形为温暖的生物机械音色垫，与FM合成器琶音和低频嗡鸣交织；中段以竖琴拨奏和经典氛围派合成器取代人声，接近Harold Budd与Laraaji的美学；第三首引入近似民谣的弦乐，吉吉·马辛式的合成器音色若隐若现。终曲在电影化弦乐与微弱节奏间维持入眠般的张力。整张专辑扎根于爵士、灵魂乐与简约主义脉络，而非当代常见的麻醉式氛围音乐，呈现出层次丰富且具深度的声音探索。

items.body:
Airbrushed, subtropical, new age ambient-jazz from Jesse Peterson’s Maui-based project, given its highest profile platform to date on Amsterdam’s Music From Memory, and warmly advised to admirers of his regular spars, Carlos Niño, Laraaji, Mia Doi Todd...

"Originally formed in New York in the late 2000s, Turn On The Sunlight has evolved into a fluid, location-spanning practice rooted in collaboration, intuition and process. Now based on Maui, Peterson’s work draws together a wide network of musicians and environments, with recordings taking shape across Los Angeles, Tokyo, London, San Miguel de Allende and Haʻikū.

Loosely situated within a framework of organic, ambient-leaning jazz, 'Iseo' unfolds as a series of open, exploratory pieces, with electronics sitting subtly beneath acoustic and environmental elements. Built from layered instrumentation including synthesizers, guitar, zither, flutes, voice and field recordings, Peterson moves between grounded, tactile detail and more expansive, immersive states. A sense of warmth and permeability runs throughout: organic percussion, environmental textures and drifting rhythmic elements lend the record a gently saturated humidity, reflecting Peterson’s base in Hawaii, where the presence of nature is felt as much as it is heard.

Underlying the project is a way of working rooted in gathering, listening and tending. Instruments, ensemble sessions, field recordings and everyday environments are approached with attentiveness, shaped through collecting, refining and allowing things to settle. Relationships, landscape and lived experience shape the sound, giving 'Iseo' a tactile, almost hand-made quality.

Rather than fixed arrangements, the album feels as if it has been organically and lovingly assembled through a process of listening and response, each element finding its place within a wider, evolving whole. This approach reaches a natural centre point in the 15-minute piece 'Medianoche En La Calle Aurora', which unfolds patiently, bending through shifting environments as motifs and textures emerge and dissolve with quiet continuity.

Peterson’s role as both instigator and facilitator is central to the project. Bringing together a diverse group of collaborators including Carlos Niño, Mia Doi Todd, Laraaji, Ko Ishikawa, Luis Pérez Ixoneztli and Miles Spilsbury, he creates space for individual voices to emerge within a shared language. The result is a music defined by openness and generosity.

'Iseo' takes its title from Peterson’s son’s middle name, a word that can be understood to mean ‘one-world life’. The piece itself takes the form of a gentle lullaby, its melody loosely shaped around the syllables of his name and sung to Peterson’s son by Luis Pérez Ixoneztli, a close collaborator whose presence across the record reflects a long-standing relationship that extends beyond the music itself.

Sleeve art and design by Michael Willis."
items._genre: ambient jazz / new age / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Jesse Peterson 的 Iseo 项目以夏威夷毛伊岛为据点，召集 Carlos Niño、Laraaji、Mia Doi Todd 等横跨洛杉矶、东京、伦敦、墨西哥的多元音乐人合作，将合成器、吉他、齐特琴、长笛、人声与田野录音层层叠合，营造出一种亚热带式的潮湿通透质感。整张专辑没有固定编排框架，而是在聆听、回应与沉淀中自然生长，15 分钟长曲《Medianoche En La Calle Aurora》是这种工作方式的集中体现，动机与音色在环境的缓慢位移中浮现又消散。专辑同名曲以 Peterson 儿子中间名命名，由 Luis Pérez Ixoneztli 哼唱为一首温柔摇篮曲，音乐中蕴含的协作、关系与生活经验赋予作品近乎手工的温度与开放性。

items.body:
Slamming, sci-fi skooled Detroit jit from the sound’s contemporary standard bearer, bolstered by a lethal Arpanet remix from Gerald Donald, whose early Dopplereffekt classics are ghettotech/jit canon.

On four brisk originals Shawscape Renegade weaves extramusical inspiration from classic sci-fi themes - existential dread; the costs of technological evolution; the dead ends of overspecialisation - into tightly coiled club motors. 

His acidic electrofunked ’78 Light Years From Earth’ pings like a Stingray zinger, and ‘Mechanise 9’ locks into a proper pneumatic 4/4 pump galvanised with gunky synths, and ‘Ignition One’ pares it all back to fluid bass hydrodynamic punctuated by the type of snares that knock your fillings out - as deployed in the Black to Techno documentary soundtrack. 

His ‘Terraformers Warning’ is a standout of inimitable 313 machine funk, but let’s be fair, Arpanet’s Quanta Remodel of the same components is just on a whole nexx level: riddled with breathless detailing, discordant synth voices and cyber-dubbed aerodynamic sleekness that will sound utterly sick on a decent rig. 

DJs beware - “the vinyl versions of A1 & B1 are five BPM slower than the digital, moving the music to between 128BPM and 151BPM on a standard Technics turntable and opening it up for play in a greater range of club environs.
items._genre: electro / ghettotech / jit / acid / Detroit techno
items._cn_summary: Shawescape Renegade 以底特律 jit/juke 为骨架，将经典科幻主题——技术进化的代价、过度专业化的死胡同、存在性焦虑——编织进紧凑的俱乐部舞曲结构。四首原创作品风格各异：酸性 electrofunk 让人联想到 Stingray 时代的锐利音色，气动 4/4 律动配合黏稠合成器线条，hydro 风格的低频与打击力极强的军鼓形成对比，整体呈现出 313 区独特的机器 funk 美学。Gerald Donald 以 Arpanet 身份操刀的 Quanta Remodel 将同一素材推至更高层次：呼吸感十足的细节编排、不和谐合成器人声与赛博 dub 的空气动力学质感并存，在优质音响系统上将释放最大能量。唱片还提供 128-151 BPM 范围内的多种速度版本以适配不同俱乐部场景，是一张兼具科幻叙事与硬核舞池功能的底特律电子作品。

items.body:
Flautist and composer Taiga Ultan joins the Kou Records roster with one of the most chilling solo flute records we've heard, recorded as usual in high def by the great Randall Dunn.

The flute is one of those instruments that's terminally misunderstood. Ancient and beautiful, it's often marginalized as a solo voice, even though it's been used in that way for quite literally thousands of years. Ultan seems to understand its historical resonance as she tracks through 'Shade Zero'. On opener 'Adagio', she acknowledges its place in classical music, offering up a virtuosic performance, but as the album creeps on, her playing is freed up, her tone more unsettling. Just listening to 'Act I', where she creates animalistic sounds and percussive flurries with the flute's keys, or 'Act II', where the instrument is turned into a vessel for her screams. 

When she introduces spoken language in the album's back half, it seems to affirm Ultan's relationship with the instrument, oddly enough. The flute is always there, but there's no sound without a voice. "Why do I think the thoughts that I think," she muses on 'Neighbors' over rainfall. The flute appears again on 'Memorial Day', but the sound has changed, dipped to an owl like hoot in the distance, way behind Ultan's words.
items._genre: experimental / contemporary classical / solo flute / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 长笛演奏家兼作曲家 Taiga Ultan 的首张个人长笛专辑，由 Randall Dunn 录制。开篇《Adagio》以古典语汇致敬传统，展示精湛演奏技艺。随后演奏逐步解放，音色变得不安：《Act I》中她用按键制造动物般声响与打击式急奏，《Act II》则将长笛转化为承载尖叫的容器。专辑后半段引入人声与念白，雨声背景下的《Neighbors》中她低语追问思维的本质，《Memorial Day》里长笛退化为远处猫头鹰般的呜咽，与人声形成空间层次。长笛贯穿始终，但声音与语言的关系被重新审视——器乐不再是独立的主体，而是与声音、人声共构的整体。这张专辑重新思考了独奏长笛的当代可能性，将其从古典附属品转化为具有实验精神的载体。

items.body:
Essential listening FFO Time Is Away, Jon Collin or the 'Bagpuss' soundtrack, Rory Salter, aka Malvern Brume, confronts cutesy British folk nostalgia on 'For Red Riverbank', using 'The Wind in the Willows' references, sobering newsreel snippets and straight-to-tape acoustic jams to develop a faded image of labour inequality.

Nostalgia is supposed to be digestible - a cultural banana that gives the mind all familiarity without friction. But munch on the same gear for too long and it starts to cause irritation; it's hard not to notice, for example, that the prim Ghost Box-style Gen Z hauntology has reached its logical conclusion. Whatever it was saying about the UK's welfare-era lost futures has not only been photocopied half to death, but it's also been added to the slop machine, spat out as empty "content" that's almost hypnotically nauseating - especially when you consider the state of welfare in 2026. Thankfully, we're not the only people to have noticed; Salter takes aim at the romance of British folk culture on his proper The Sprigs debut, using a framework we'll all be familiar with - Kenneth Grahame's Edwardian children's classic 'The Wind in the Willows'. It's important to note that the book was already steeped in nostalgia when it was first published back in 1908, a reflection on nature in the face of mass industrialization, as the affordable Ford Model T was beginning to appear on roads for the first time. So it's a more complex reference than you might initially figure, and Salter uses this backdrop to root his investigation of British labour history and the very meaning of tradition.

We've all heard remnants of folk music vibrate through the collective consciousness over the years, not least in the wake of the New Weird America movement of the early '00s. And Salter's awareness of these sounds and the perpetual churn that followed is crucial; he doesn't subvert them as such, but repurposes them, hitting on themes and sequences that connect us to the country's soil and textures that help to rub away some of nostalgia's entrancing sparkle. The 12-minute opener 'come along, back home' sounds at first like an old protestant hymn being bellowed through broken pipes and Salter keeps scraping away at history, collaging textured environmental loops with simplistic, almost naive folk songs, peculiar resonances and, occasionally, what sounds like an old recorder. And it's the back-and-forth between gravelly noise and nostalgic naivety that makes 'For Red Riverbank' so inviting. The short, sharp 'Ratty & the moles get to work' is just as jolly as its title, sounding as brittle and evocative as Sandra Kerr and John Faulkner's fluttered folk songs that lifted Oliver Postgate's 'Bagpuss'.

And Salter doesn't just look back through rose-tinted spectacles, he juxtaposes these evocative sounds with sobering recordings of newsreaders, politicians and union leaders, who complete a quite genuine picture of the recent past. Like George Eliot's Middlemarch, that imagined a fictional Midlands town four decades prior to its writing, the inviting idealized setting was a Trojan horse for Eliot's real theme: the 1832 Reform Act that upended the electoral system. Salter employs the same sleight of hand, introducing us to a world we know and love before drip, drip, dripping the politics we so desperately need.
items._genre: experimental folk / hauntology / collage / acoustic improvisation / field recording
items._cn_summary: Rory Salter以The Sprigs之名推出的首张专辑，以肯尼斯·格雷厄姆的《柳林风声》为框架，挖掘英国民俗文化中潜藏的怀旧政治。专辑将直录原声民谣、环境循环录音、复古竖笛独奏与新闻播报、工会领袖演说等史料拼贴并置，在粗粝噪音与天真民歌之间反复切换。12分钟开场曲以破损管风琴般的质感演绎古老赞美诗，后续短曲则以脆弱而轻盈的民谣段落呼应《巴格巴斯》配乐风格。专辑并非简单颠覆民谣传统，而是重新利用其音色与序列，剥离怀旧的糖衣，呈现一幅关于英国劳工历史与自然消逝的复杂图景。

"Recorded in the winter of 1981/82 between rehearsal space, provincial disco and bar nights, and a humble four-track setup, these tracks capture the raw spirit of a generation that simply started creating—no formal training, but plenty of attitude. Minimalist, uncompromising, and inspired by krautrock, punk, new wave, elect
items.body:
44 years after its original release, the 7” by German group DEUTSCHE SCHÄFERHUNDE (engl. German shepherds) - remastered and reissued for the first time on Anna Logue Records.

"Recorded in the winter of 1981/82 between rehearsal space, provincial disco and bar nights, and a humble four-track setup, these tracks capture the raw spirit of a generation that simply started creating—no formal training, but plenty of attitude. Minimalist, uncompromising, and inspired by krautrock, punk, new wave, electronic music and dub, the songs move between raw electronics, percussive noise, new wave experimentation, and sharp social commentary. „Rosa Brille“ (rose coloured glasses) in particular feels as urgent today as it did back then—a track that has lost none of its relevance, „Gasmasken“ tells of gas masks dancing in the woods to the sound of sirens, and a timeless Holger Czukay/Jah Wobble inspired „Mein Herz“ (my heart).

Originally pressed in a small run of just 500 copies and later becoming a sought-after collector’s item now worth 200€, the record now returns in a carefully crafted edition featuring a laser-printed reverse side and additional materials such as original lyric sheets and articles, postcard and poster. DEUTSCHE SCHÄFERHUNDE thrived on paradox—a provocative name paired with a clear stance, and lyrics that still resonate today. Shaped by Cold War tension, political unease, and youthful rebellion, their sound refused to fit into any neat category. Only few other bands, such as Der Musikant, Im Namen des Volkes, Thorax Wach, Klinisch Sauber oder Stephan Eicher spielt Noise Boys come to mind."
items._genre: post-punk / krautrock / new wave / electronic / dub-influenced
items._cn_summary: 这张1981至1982年间由德国乐队录制的7寸单曲集，经安娜·洛格唱片厂牌重新母带处理并再版发行。乐队在排练室与迪斯科酒吧之间，用简陋的四轨设备完成了这些作品，没有任何正规音乐训练，纯粹凭借态度与冲劲进行创作。音乐融合了德国泡菜摇滚的冷峻骨架、朋克的直接态度、新浪潮的实验精神、电子音乐的冰冷质感以及对杜比混音的借鉴，在原始电子声响、打击乐噪音与锐利的社会评论之间游走。《Rosa Brille》讽刺玫瑰色眼镜式的乐观主义，时至今日依然切中要害；《Gasmasken》描绘防毒面具在森林中伴着警报起舞的场景；而《Mein Herz》则展现出霍尔格·楚克与贾·沃布尔式的深沉律动。原版仅压制500张，如今已成为身价200欧的收藏珍品。此次再版不仅包含激光印刷的盘面，还附赠原始歌词手稿、海报与明信片等文献资料，完整呈现了冷战阴影下德国青年一代的反叛语境。

items.body:
Real heart-stopping, life-affirming, almost indescribably beautiful posthumous album featuring (for the first time) vocal works by beloved, dearly departed, Ethiopian nun and now-legendary pianist/composer Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru, room recorded straight to tape between 1977-1985, sounds of life just about audible in the background. Almost had an out of body experience listening to it the other night - just a perfect, 10/10 album.

’Souvenirs’ is an intimate self-portrait written, recorded and compiled by the late Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru; a classically-trained pianist turned nun, whose singular style of jazz and blues-inflected composition and performance became globally renowned in her latter years via reissues and compilations reaching as far back as the 1960s, namely the ‘Éthiopiques 21: Piano Solo’ CD and a much-prized eponymous set in 2016. At the age of 99, Emahoy passed away in Jerusalem last year, whilst planning towards this first ever showcase of her vocals - which have never appeared on her purely piano-based recordings until now, making for a truly life-affirming experience from its opening bars. 

The posthumous release, realised in collaboration with Emahoy’s family and Mississippi Records - is a stone cold stunner. It grants unprecedented access to her discrete craft and inner world in Addis Ababa, against a backdrop of the Ethiopian Red Terror and Civil War, prior to her subsequent exile in a Jerusalem convent. Whilst all no doubt defined by her signature, intricate and lilting type of classical meets jazz-blues phrasing, the eight songs are all far more concise than her usual instrumental works, made even more spellbinding by the revelation of her softly contoured and captivating vocals that beautifully trace and overlie the cadence of her keys. It’s just pure, unbridled expression that’s only heightened by the seemingly off-the-cuff nature of the recordings, as if she just sung the songs to herself, impromptu, never intended for public consumption.

Replete with incidental creaks of the piano stool, birds outside the window, and Emahoy’s finger on the record button, the songs depict themes of loss, mourning and soon-to-be exile, sung into a basic boombox. They place us in the room with her, closer than ever, privy to a vocal version of the closing number to her eponymous compilation, now unveiled as a dedication her niece, the titular Tenkou, with lyrics to guide her adulthood “Don’t cry / Childhood won’t come back / Let it go with love”, alongside the beatific, open-window paean ‘Clouds Moving on the Sky’, and melancholic hiraeth of ‘Ethiopia My Homeland’ or ‘Don’t Forget Your Country’, and ineffable, humbling elegance of idea and execution to ‘Is It Sunny or Cloudy in the Land You Live?’ and ‘Where is the Highway of Thought?’.

Unmissable.
items._genre: Ethiopian piano / vocal jazz-blues / classical / world music
items._cn_summary: 这张遗作收录了埃塞俄比亚修女钢琴家兼作曲家Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru于1977至1985年间用磁带录制的八首作品，首次将人声纳入此前纯器乐的创作框架。录音以盒式录音机直接在房间内完成，保留了琴凳吱呀声、窗外鸟鸣与按录音键的杂音，营造出强烈的在场感。作品融合古典钢琴语法与爵士蓝调语汇，人声轻柔地铺陈于琴键节奏之上，主题围绕失落、哀悼与流亡展开，包括献给侄女的多首短歌以及对故土的怀念篇章。这张专辑由Mississippi Records与其家人合作发行，是对其离散经历与内在世界的私密呈现。

items.body:
Danish composer Astrid Sonne opens up her heart on 'Great Doubt', singing candidly for the first time over powdery beats and jerky instrumentation (assisted by none other than Slauson Malone, Ben Vince, Levitation Orchestra's Emma Barnaby and Alvilda Reiter Jakobsen), and even referencing Mariah Carey. It's a revelation - and funny in places too - properly in line with Tirzah, ML Buch and HTRK.

We almost didn't recognize Sonne when we first spun 'Great Doubt'. Her voice - not her viola or rack of synths - takes the spotlight on 'Do you wanna', murmuring gently over brittle, tightly reverberating drums that Sonne plays herself. It's a far cry from the pitchy, jazz-inflected psychedelia of 2021's 'outside of your lifetime' or its vaporous predecessor 'Human Lines'. "Do you wanna have a baby?" she asks ruefully, leaving the question unanswered at first, room for strings, piano and subtle synths to reply. She strips herself naked, wondering what it might mean to bring a child into the world; it scrapes against Tirzah's 'Colourgrade' not just sonically but thematically. On that album, Tirzah contemplated motherhood and family - here, Sonne weighs up her choices, using the track's emptiness to suggest emotional malnutrition. "I don't know," she finally relents.

'Give my all' follows with boxy, disney strings and orchestral phrases that bring an uncanny drama to Sonne's blunt words. She sounds confident and forthright as she paraphrases Maria Carey: "I'd give my all to have / just one more night with you." The plasticity of the backdrop only makes the words resonate further, and it's this push and pull between artificiality and raw sensitivity that makes 'Great Doubt' so captivating. There's an unmistakable trip-hop impetus to 'Boost', that features Sonne on drums again, playing slowly alongside sampled woodwinds and fictile synths. There are no vocals on this one, so the instrumentation stands in, winding in and out of tune to poke out towards the boundaries. It's at this moment when Sonne sounds closest to her sometime collaborator ML Buch, bridging the gap between traditional songwriting and a simulated new age. But Sonne doesn't sound as if she's trying to approximate pop, just bare her soul more frankly.

And there are traces of her earlier material on the stand-out 'Staying here', when she coos more animatedly over organ-like arpeggios and digitized stabs. We can hear outlines of classic Enya or Kate Bush on this one, and while it's beatless, it sounds as if it's rushing towards a drop that never comes - all tension, no release. "Everything is unreal," she cries. "But I'm not going anywhere." Then we're led out with the folk-y 'Overture', that features Ben Vince on sax, and dubby closer 'Say you love me', the biggest indicator that she's now based in London. It's the most revealing, heart-puncturing material we've heard from Sonne to date, a hyper-literate wirework of influences and skills that's put together with care and no small amount of restraint. We're sold.
items._cn_summary: 丹麦作曲家Astrid Sonne在这张专辑中首次亲自献声，告别了此前以中提琴和合成器为主导的爵士迷幻路线。她自己演奏鼓机，叠加脆弱的人声与盒装弦乐、塑料质感的合成器音墙，歌词涉及生育焦虑、情感空虚等私密主题。制作上邀请Slauson Malone、Ben Vince、Levitation Orchestra成员等多位跨界音乐人合作，在trip-hop骨架上融入Enya式的管风琴琶音、Kate Bush式的声乐线条，以及dub和trip-hop的律动。专辑在人工感与原始脆弱之间反复拉扯，与Tirzah、ML Buch、HTRK等当代艺术流行场景形成呼应，是她迄今最袒露内心、也最具文学感的作品。

items.body:
Simon Shreeve (Mønic, CUB) sifts and tweaks nine personal highlights of his cult transition from D&B to dubstep circa the late ‘00s/early 2010s, all acutely advised to acolytes of Youngsta, SP:MC, Icicle, Raime, The Bug x Ghost Dubs, Mick Harris...

By the time Kryptic Minds switched from darkest D&B to dubstep in 2009, they were arguably late to the game, but heavily made their presence felt with a five year string of classics for Loefah’s Swamp81, Tectonic, and their own label, Osiris Music UK, now considered canon to the sound. ‘The Things They Left Behind’ now dusts off and refines nine crucial examples of how they brought D&B production values to the heel of its rogue sibling, dubstep, firmly living up to El-B’s original dream of fusing late ‘90s tech-step and darker UKG, but also augmented with careful measures of atmospheric trip hop sensuality that place it in the long shadow of UK gloom shrouding Burial and Pinch bits.

Basically it’s a director’s cut of 2011 album ‘Can’t Sleep’, all “reimagined, refined and 2026 remastered” to best tell his tale of that pivotal era. In passage from the pensive title tune to cinematic closer ‘1000 Lost Cities’, he tightens the screws and checks the brakes on a definitive redux, edging the rictus halfstep tension of ‘No More No Less’, and a spidery 2-step dissection ‘Alone’, along with the relatively sublime levity of ‘Fade to Nothing’, and what sounds like ‘Mezzanine’-era Massive Attack gone halfstep on ‘Myth’, thru to the digitally shivered delays of ‘Depth of Field’ and slicker retread of ‘A Glimpse of Hope’.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Kryptic Minds从Drum & Bass转向Dubstep关键时期作品的精选重制版，由Mønic成员Simon Shreeve亲自挑选并重新混音。素材源自2011年专辑《Can't Sleep》中的九首作品，经过重新构想与精炼，并进行2026年高清重制，以更完整地呈现那个转折时代的音乐脉络。编曲将DnB的制作精度注入dubstep的低频骨架，融合九十年代末tech-step与暗黑UK Garage的基因，同时融入trip-hop式氛围质感，呼应Burial与Pinch所代表的英国阴郁美学。作品在半步节奏的张力与电影叙事感之间游走，标题曲沉思开场，收尾曲《1000 Lost Cities》则具有戏剧性收束感，中间穿插半步碎拍紧张感、蛛网式2-step解构以及Massive Attack式的阴冷质地。这是一份具有历史档案价值与厂牌美学深度的策划性重制，适合关注英国地下低音电子场景演变的听众。

items.body:
Gary Sullivan, host of WFMU's Bodega Pop, pools his Brooklyn and Queens finds on this crunchy anthology, collecting early 20th century Russian music that was prized by first-generation Russian New Yorkers.

Time's frozen on 'Let Me Perish Without Return', a set of noisy ballads, music hall standards and folky reflections that map out the experience of the diaspora who immigrated from the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union as the home they knew transformed beyond recognition. Sullivan combed thrift stores in Forest Hills, Brighton Beach and Gravesend to find these intriguing cues, and pieces together a story that's shared by half a million New Yorkers. The remnants of Russian life are still visible on the surface of these neighborhoods, and the music helps us understand the culture a little more deeply. It's not particularly familiar material, but it makes for fascinating listening - especially if you've rinsed the rest of the Death is Not the End catalog.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由WFMU电台主持人Gary Sullivan策划，汇集了1889至1917年间从俄罗斯帝国流散至纽约布鲁克林与皇后区的第一代移民所珍视的早期录音，涵盖嘈杂的民谣、歌舞厅标准曲与带有乡愁色彩的音乐作品。Sullivan在Forest Hills、Brighton Beach和Gravesend的旧货店中发掘这些被遗忘的唱片，试图还原一个半纽约人共同经历的离散故事。合辑记录了帝国衰亡与故土剧变背景下移民群体的文化记忆，音乐本身带有粗粝的年代质感与强烈的地域辨识度。作为Death is Not the End厂牌发行的档案式汇编，它面向熟悉该厂牌其他冷门挖掘项目的听众，将社区表面残存的俄罗斯文化痕迹转化为可聆听的历史文献。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. items._cn_summary: 巴西音乐人Lucas Santtana在其第九张专辑《Brasiliano》中，以巴西葡萄牙语（Brasiliano）为核心概念，展开对巴西多元文化与语言历史的音乐探索。专辑以葡萄牙语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及土著图皮-瓜拉尼语演唱，邀请包括Gilberto Gil在内的多国客座词曲作者与歌手参与。开篇曲以巴西葡语女性化形象隐喻语言演变史，提炼土著词汇融入日常文化。编曲融合人声、弦乐、钢琴、吉他、mellotron与合成器，呈现层次丰富且温暖的声场。风格跨越派对曲、雷鬼、法式香颂与简约吉他弹唱，承载文化互鉴与政治表达的意图，是一张兼具语言学趣味与音乐多元性的世界音乐作品。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

items.body: Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka I n the High Middle Ages, Hildegard of Bingen said that �The truly holy person welcomes all that is earthly.� William Blake declared in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790) that �Exuberance is beauty.� In 1855, Walt Whitman published the poem �Song Of Myself, 51� in Leaves of Grass , which contains the famous line �I am large, I contain multitudes.� I�m just skimming the surface of mystical experience, of those struck by wonder and an all-encompassing insight into how people fit into the �grand scheme of things.� At some point on this trajectory, the boundary between the religious and the secular breaks down and simply being human becomes the ultimate wow. Which brings us to Polish artist Maria Ka�s latest album Di Mashin . Ka found that her family had Jewish roots, a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. As on 2023�s Der Hemshekh , she unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical, and she presents us with a whole Yiddish cosmos. While not sharing the same type of musical style, Ka reminds me of John Zorn�s aesthetic of mixing the grotesque and the sacred into Jewish experimental music. She also reminds me of the woman on the phone sampled on Wally Brill�s Jewish cantorial electronica album The Covenant (2007), who confesses she can�t sleep after hearing someone in a bar talking about the Book of Ezekiel and being haunted by the vision of Jews arriving from a future space-time. She sees that we are all suspended in webs of relationships. She is also deeply aware of how we are subject to larger social forces and structures � which sometimes must be met with radical action -- that are the machinery of life. There is a heavy dose of electro and punkish attitude spinning through her musical universe. Ostensibly, the album is divided between electronic and rock tracks, but there is a consistency to the sound that is united in loopy joy. At its best, Di Mashin is sly and sexy. Opening track �Alef � Tsentauri Disko� finds Ka in the city, musing on the seaside, wriggling like a snake at night, and watching Gdańsk wake up. �I often Dream about Cosmos, about the Land above the Earth / overhead / Alef Centauri Jewish disco!� she sings, set to a thumping urban electro grind. (See video below) Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �Vos iz dos?� is a standout, more in the �rock� vein, with Ka howling a debate over the Yiddish language itself. Perhaps it is based in a critique that she received, as she starts with What is this? Maria, what is this? I constantly hear it, it has not finished You speak no Yiddish!/ It�s so easy! Your language is incorrect, mistaken is your speech and dialect! � Given that Ka is producing new modern songs in Yiddish, there is something disarming in acknowledging the tension over who might claim ownership of language itself. Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �SuperNove� might remind listeners of Jacob wrestling with God, if that battle was done to an �80s new wave beat. Ka has visions of the past, the Old World and old demons, and she fights a ghost that rises to block her way: � I fought him with Strength, punched him with my both hands�I triumphed over him! I myself � I did triumph over him! � And after that victory, � it�s a great Surprise � the Past melted in the Cosmic Blast! � Ka also seems to be challenging herself, pointing in new directions. �Di Kosmish motorn (Cosmic engines)� brought to mind the former Warsaw Village Band�s blues-influenced singer Maja Kleszcz. Depeche Mode�s (fronted by Dave Gahan, of Jewish ancestry) forays into fusing electronica with blues might be another touchpoint. Hearing the cosmic engines like a modern day Pythagoras, she is awestruck by hearing the cosmic engines in her head. �Dos geverk (The mechanism)� offers some grinding guitars to convey the constant motion of the daily rat race � echoed later on by the title track, �Di Mashin (The Machine),� which peels back the layers of society to reveal the incessant obsession for money. The music of �The Machine� is hyperspeed cabaret, close to madness. The system demands more money � but she indicates that she is a spanner in the works, working to bring it down: � I watch the machine�s death / Full and steadily red is my hand in the end. � Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka Feminist politics come to the fore on �Ikh bin a froy (I am a woman),� and Ka reminds me a bit of the divine Ms. H of Bingen chanting over a motoric beat. She refuses to be hemmed in by structures, signaling that the Forest is her home, the stars her friends; �I wake up every day / and new scroll create.� Album closer �Di milkhome� (War)� is more future blues, transposing war, empty shipyards, and advice from her mother that all miseries will end and freedom will navigate the turmoil �like huge ships at Sea.� Di Mashin is possessed by such a singular offbeat vision and personal mythology that I wonder where Maria Ka will take her Yiddishfuturism next�Perhaps beyond our solar system, grooving on an interstellar plane with her band wriggling like snakes. Find the artist online. Further listening: Maria Ka - Der Hemshekh Warsaw Village Band & Bassałyki - Sploty WoWaKin - Kraj za miastem

items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items.body: sMiLes by Jowee Omicil B orn in Montreal, Haitian-Canadian musician-composer Jowee Omicil plays a fabulous variety of saxophones, clarinets, trumpets, flutes, piano, and keyboards. He came of age in the choral milieu of his father�s Montreal congregation, studied saxophone and music education at Berklee, and gleaned much from engagement with figures including Wyclef Jean, Tony Allen, Ibrahim Maalouf, Roy Hargrove, Kenny Garrett, Pharoah Sanders, Branford Marsalis, and Marcus Miller among others. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released sMiLes one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast. The album opens with a striking reinterpretation of singer and Civil Rights activist Abbey Lincoln�s �Throw It Away,� whose message Omicil invokes in his voiceover, an expression of kinship in creative philosophical outlook. (For good measure, Omicil revisits the title on a distinctive �Throw it Away - FuLL oF LoVe Remix.�) Lincoln�s own 2007 rendition on Abbey Sings (Verve) offers critical context, itself worth a comparative audition for the original melody and the contemplative character of her lyrics. Throw it away, throw it away Give your love, live your life, each and every day And keep your hand wide open, let the sun shine through, Because you can never lose a thing, if it belongs to you. In less accomplished hands, the quirky sampling, effects, instrumentation, and wide-ranging, scruffy, sonic bricolage of sMiLes could make for one muddy m�lange. But no danger lies here in Jowee�s paradoxical, provocative, sound-shifting extended groove. Omicil's voice and sax blend almost imperceptibly in �SOeuR FeLiX AKA BeeHive.� In �Trip to GHanA,� polyrhythm meets wah-tone high-life guitar, cackly sax, and wordless vocalise. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes by Jowee Omicil Feat. Mawuena Kodjovi Other titles transport the listener to Haiti, Morocco, Cape Verde, Jupiter, and Mali. �LeTTre Du MALi PouR JonaTHan� is a meditative, revelatory piano solo nearly ten minutes in length. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes may invoke the free-blowing spirit of Miles (as on the sound-effected �MiLes ConvoY�), but there is no anxiety of influence here. Far from a rote genuflection to musical antecedents, the prevailing voice throughout is purely Omicil�s. As he counsels, �trust the note.� "Seek for the sound that is within you and the [instrument] will drive you to your destination� the singularity of sound is what I have always been searching for, the sound that comes from the heart, the sound that maybe, perhaps, is only heard in nature, this is what we are looking for when we are talking about sound� deep down, heartfelt uniqueness, always connected with the spirits�" - Jowee Omicil In accord with his music education formation, Omicil also leads music workshops through his BasH! AkademY, �a close-knit setting embracing spontaneity, authenticity, and shared growth,� which in 2025 included �a nomadic music experience traveling the world� to Mindelo, Cabo Verde. In 2026 Omicil will perform in New York, Canada, Martinique, France, Germany, Austria, Poland, Romania, the UK, and an African tour in the planning stage.
