items.body: For more than three decades, Ataraxia has been regarded as both a household name and a cult act within the broad realms of Ethereal, Neo-Classical, Folk, and related musical genres. Throughout the years, Ataraxia’s core members – Francesca Nicoli, Vittorio Vandelli, and Giovanni Pagliari – have remained driven by an inexhaustible source of inspiration, deeply rooted in their spiritual experience. Of course, their remarkable talent plays a vital role, but so does the authenticity that consistently shines through in their compositions. Ataraxia offers a genuine remedy – perhaps even an antidote – to a world that rushes by like a bullet train. Ataraxia embodies reflection and wisdom, a profound love of nature, and a deep respect for ancient traditions, legends, and myths. With their latest album, “Sylfaera The Fair”, released through the Greek label The Circle Music and serving as the concluding chapter of a new trilogy, Ataraxia once again affirm not only their artistic brilliance but also the sincerity and integrity that define their approach to music. For me, Ataraxia’s “Sylfaera The Fair” is a truly immersive experience – one in which spirituality and artistry become inseparable. I had the pleasure of discussing the album and much more with Francesca Nicoli. (Courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) Ataraxia interview Q: Ataraxia was formed almost 40 years ago, and your latest album marks the thirtieth full-length release in this impressive journey. How do you look back on the young artists you were in the 1980s, and what has remained the common thread throughout this long career? Francesca: The first Ataraxia album was born in 1990, 36 years ago. We cannot describe a thirty-six-year process because we are always looking toward the so-called future; we are always looking ahead to what we will do. It has been such a fast, intense, and prolific flow that we are unable to find descriptive phrases that allow us to reflect on the complete body of work, because this is nothing other than the complete work of our life brought into music. We remember the experiences and enthusiasm of concerts around the world, the recording of the albums, but our emotions and vision are all directed toward what will be. Perhaps one day, a listener will be able to outline the path; we are the same people who have lived thirty different lives, so by necessity, we are others while maintaining that original root. It is as if we had been reincarnated 30 times in different bodies while maintaining the same soul that discovers new possibilities every time. Q: “Sylfaera The Fair” is the final part of an Ataraxia trilogy preceded by “Pomegranate” (2022) and “Centaurea” (2024). Did you know from the very beginning that it was going to be a trilogy, or did this happen more along the way? And what does this final opus represent, and how should listeners approach the trilogy as a whole? Francesca: We didn’t know it for sure, but we felt it; we knew it would end this way because we have always worked in trilogies throughout our career. It represents a part of our life in a mythological key, and therefore accessible to all and useful to everyone, like any form of art, to sublimate the meaning of existence for those who listen to it. The right approach is simply to listen to it in order, or even in reverse—from the third album to the first—and let the images that accompany the listening bloom, take the journey, enjoy the journey, and see how one comes out transformed by all this. A musical listening is always a journey, and from no journey nobody returns the same and to the same place. Q: Trilogies originated in antiquity, and I remain fascinated by how this format continues to evolve today. What fascinates you personally about the trilogy form, the symbols (like the number 9 in this album) in it and are there any examples from the wider art world that have particularly inspired or moved you? Francesca: The number three is a peculiar number, the number of perfection and communication. Cycles are completed that start from one, which also corresponds to the sign of Aries, and therefore to birth, the initial force that brings life to bloom and utter its first cry. Then, two is the mirror; we are in front of another who reflects our essence—without which we would not know who we are—up to the completeness of three, which is communication and creation, because from the union of two is born; the son, or what is created; by the energy of the two, becoming something new. Needless to say, Tolkien has always inspired us, and Tolkien also worked with the trilogy. But there are also references in painting and an interesting numerological studies we did years ago. Nine is the maximum expression of three (3×3), and nine are the characters of the album who will find themselves energetically creating “Sylfaera The Fair”, the realm of music, beauty, and harmony. Nine is the Hermit of the Tarot, the one who in solitude carries the lamp of knowledge on a path backwards, walking toward the past, in retrocausality. Then we have the Tesla sequence 3-6-9, which is a complement of mathematical and philosophical awareness that has always fascinated us. Q: I believe it is fair to say that mysticism has always played a central role in Ataraxia‘s musical universe and that it also reflects something about the people behind the artists. How important is the mystical dimension in your daily lives, and how do you perceive mysticism in the contemporary Western world, where it seems to be gradually disappearing? Francesca: We were born with this mystical nature, and since we were children, we have lived experiences linked to subtle worlds, amplified by life in medieval villages or on the Apennines of our region. Woods, rivers, mountains, and undoubtedly our numerous experiences on the Greek islands, as well as those on the Italian peaks, have created the substrate—the most powerful means—to experience our music in a mystical state. The mystical dimension in everyday life is still our nature; it is not a specific moment we dedicate ourselves to, it is the very way in which we perceive life and our experiences. We struggle to give you explanations regarding the disappearance of mysticism in the contemporary Western world because we live things from the inside; we exist in this dimension 24 hours a day, and this is our lens. In a certain way, staying within this dimension protects us—otherwise, we would not be able to write music, to feel in a certain way, or to imagine a profound bond between everything and between this and other possible dimensions. For us, mysticism is nothing more than feeling a profound connection, at both a cellular level and a higher mental level, to the heart of things, to the heart of a greater design that gives meaning to this earthly experience. A profound sensitivity is necessary, which can be wounded by the prosaic nature of life, and we must take care of it every day. Q: Ataraxia’s music often evokes ancient civilizations, forgotten rituals, and a sacred experience of nature, an atmosphere strengthened by the use of traditional instruments. How essential is this approach to your artistic identity, and how do you view modern music culture and the rise of AI, which in some ways seems to represent its opposite? Francesca: The nature of our music is as you describe; this approach is essential to be able to express ourselves in an honest, authentic way, which can bring forth sincere suggestions. Our creativity is indomitable, so we do not need ‘external intelligences’; due to a lack of inspiration; furthermore, we have been in the musical world for so many years that we feel no need for it at all. We like working with new sounds (natural and synthesized), but not delegating. We like having the responsibility for what we do, being the conductors of the orchestra, and using and refining our musical intelligence in order to remain operative and lucid. We don’t set ourselves against something; we act creatively to create something. Q: Speaking of traditional instruments, “Sylfaera The Fair” is once again an absolute masterpiece and a true tour de force, featuring contributions from guest musicians. How do you bring such an ambitious undertaking to life, and what does the composition process look like in practice? Francesca: For us, it is completely natural because every time, fellow musician friends arrive who integrate into the new project and the new album in a completely spontaneous way, and everything flows. We don’t have to tell them what to do or what not to do; they intuit it perfectly and create their melodies, blending their musical experience with our suggestions. Then, we work with great concentration on the rhythmic parts because we create them ourselves; these create the earth upon which the air and the water of the instruments move, and the fire—the Flame—is the union of all these forces in harmony, working toward a single goal: the creation of the specific dimension of this musical micro-universe that’s the album. Q: Were there any specific innovations or evolutions in the choice of instruments or in the overall production process during the creation of this trilogy and especially the latest album? Francesca: The first album of the trilogy, “Pomegranate”, utilized the simplicity of our essential instruments: classical and electric guitar, keyboards, cello, and voice, with few rhythmic patterns. It was an essential and poetic album. The second album of the trilogy, “Centaurea”, became enriched with more complex arrangements while maintaining the same instruments, to which drum patterns of a certain importance were added, varying the musical suggestions as we explored different genres (Folk ballads, Neo-Classical arias, more symphonic tracks, Dream-Pop, etc.). The new album focuses on a first part more closely linked to Nordic and Mediterranean Folk, introducing uilleann pipes, bodhrán, flutes, massive tribal percussion, and choirs, while the second part is more in line with our previous releases. Q: After releasing 30 Ataraxia albums, I wonder whether there are still artists or records that continue to inspire you. More broadly, what do inspiration and creativity mean when you have devoted so many years to the same artistic project? How have these concepts evolved for you over time, and how do you continue to nurture them? Francesca: Certainly, there are artists who inspire us greatly; they don’t directly inspire our music, but rather our soul. We are always listening to new music that we discover along the way, and music remains the soundtrack of our emotions. Since we were children, we have experienced creativity as a form of expression, as the natural nourishment of our own existences, and so now we are that expression—it is our DNA. Music is our language, our universe, our way of communicating with ourselves and with what surrounds us. Everything has evolved along with our life experiences, our maturity, our spiritual search, our sufferings, and our discoveries. We nourish it simply by living and experiencing the universe of life. Q: Glossolalia, or the use of imaginary language, has long played a role in your work and seems to fit naturally within the spiritual dimension of Ataraxia. How do you approach this practice creatively? Does it require a particular form of introspection, meditation, or discipline, and have you noticed an evolution in this aspect of your work over the years? Francesca: I have always used different ancient and modern languages in my lyrics, and there has always been a track in glossolalia on every album. Each language I used was chosen for the peculiarity of its sound, which suited that specific piece of music, and from there, the step to glossolalia is a short one. Usually, I listen to the compositions the band proposes and instinctively work on the vocal melodies, which already have a specific color connected to particular sounds. It is like a meditative process: I close my eyes, listen, and the sounds come out one after the other without any particular construction—they emerge spontaneously. It seems like a magical process; in reality, the voice becomes like a musical instrument that produces sounds articulated into words. The technique has been the same since the beginning, only in this latest album it was used much more extensively compared to the previous ones. Q: What are the current short-term plans for Ataraxia, and what can we expect from the band in the longer term? Francesca: In the short term, we are working on the live performance of this album experience—each time different, each time linked to the venue and the situation in which we will be performing. In the long term, we do not know yet. Everything is revealed to us along the path, just like breathing: we inhale, just as when releasing an album, we inhale to recharge with oxygen, which will allow us to exhale a new opus once again. About Ataraxia Ataraxia is a neoclassical dark wave and dark folk band from Modena and Reggio Emilia in northern Italy. The group was founded in the second half of the 1980s by vocalist Francesca Nicoli and guitarist Michele Urbano, with the line-up stabilising around Nicoli, guitarist and composer Vittorio Vandelli, and keyboardist Giovanni Pagliari in the early 1990s. Their work combines electronic technology with archaic and acoustic instruments, and their lyrics frequently reference nature, ancient cultures and mythological themes, often performed in historically resonant locations. In their first years Ataraxia issued self-released recordings such as “Prophetia” and “Nosce Te Ipsum” before working with labels including Energeia and Cruel Moon International, gradually building an extensive discography across cassette, CD and vinyl formats. Late-1990s albums such as “Historiae” explored medieval and liturgical atmospheres; the album was later issued by Ark Records and documented both studio and live recordings, including material captured in a medieval court in 1998. During the 2000s the band continued to refine its blend of neoclassical, ethereal and folk-influenced material on releases like “Suenos” and “Os Cavaleiros do Templo,” with several titles later revisited. Twilight Records reissued long-deleted works including “Saphir” and “Os Cavaleiros do Templo.” In 2016 Ataraxia released “Deep Blue Firmament” via Sleaszy Rider Records. Subsequent full-lengths included “Synchronicity Embraced” (2018) and “Quasar” (stylised as “ΘUASAR”). The collaboration with The Circle Music began with the 28th studio album “Pomegranate (The Chant of the Elementals)”, released in 2022 on digital, CD and vinyl formats. Ahead of that album the band issued several videos, including “Hlara Aralh” and “Aura Magi.” Pomegranate – The Chant Of The Elementals by Ataraxia Ataraxia’s 29th studio album “Centaurea” followed in 2024, again on The Circle Music in digital, CD and vinyl editions. Singles and videos from this period included “The Source,” “Galen,” “Viriditas,” “Coelestis” and “Ignis Pater.” Centaurea by Ataraxia And now there is the band’s 30th album “Sylfaera the Fair”.
items._cn_summary: Ataraxia是一支来自意大利的组合，三十余年来在空灵、新古典、民谣及暗潮等交汇地带持续创作。最新专辑《Sylfaera The Fair》由希腊独立厂牌The Circle Music发行，承接前作《Pomegranate》与《Centaurea》，构成三部曲的终章。乐队核心成员Francesca Nicoli、Vittorio Vandelli与Giovanni Pagliari以精神体验为创作根基，将古老传说、自然意象与神话叙事融入声乐与器乐编排中。文章以采访形式展开，Nicoli谈到乐队始终面向未来而非回顾，将每张专辑视为同一灵魂在不同载体中的重生。《Sylfaera》延续了乐队对古老传统与现代美学的连接，但文中信息因采访文本被截断而不够完整，难以深入评判具体的声音设计或曲目结构。整体而言，这是一支具有跨类型底蕴的长期创作组合，文章呈现的更多是其艺术哲学而非音乐细节。

items.body: Aesthetische, the Brazilian electronic duo, released the digital EP “Every Beat Matters” on June 26, 2026 through Alfa Matrix. The “Every Beat Matters” EP collects four tracks and three remixes of “Chew The Loop”, and carries an explicit anti-extremism message. Aesthetische bring a sound that mixes EBM, industrialized future pop and dancefloor electronics, with machine rhythms, synth hooks and forceful vocals. Gui Pires and Fab Viscardi cite Front Line Assembly and Front 242 as touchstones. Every Beat Matters EP by AESTHETISCHE Aesthetische’s ‘Every Beat Matters’: tracks and message “Every Beat Matters” runs four tracks – “Break The State”, “Thirty Two Percent”, “Chew The Loop” and “Parallel Worlds” – followed by three remixes of “Chew The Loop”: the “beat the loop remix”, a “shortmix version” and the “spit the loop mix”. Alfa Matrix previewed “Chew The Loop” on its compilation “Sounds From The Matrix 026”, released on June 19, 2026. The EP ties its title to a stance against authoritarian rhetoric, fascism, war and prejudice, framing “every beat matters” as a call for awareness, resistance and unity; the campaign artwork carries the lines “Extremism has no place here” and “FCK NZS”. The label describes the record as turning “a simple message into a powerful call for awareness, resistance and unity.” The theme follows earlier Aesthetische records: the 2022 album “rvprty” was issued as a stand against far-right, anti-science and anti-democratic movements. About Aesthetische Aesthetische is the project of Brazilian musicians Gui Pires and Fab Viscardi, both previously in the electro-industrial act Aghast View. The duo formed this project in 2012 and have released through the Belgian label Alfa Matrix since their debut. Their albums include “Powerswitch” (2012), “HybridCore” (2014), “Co3xist3ns3” (2019) and “rvprty” (2022), alongside a run of EPs and singles. In recent years the duo released the EP “Confidence Is Silent” in 2024 and the EP “Selling Fear” in 2025, the latter also drawing on the legacy of Front Line Assembly and Front 242. Aesthetische have also discussed their approach with Side-Line in a 2024 interview. “Every Beat Matters”, released on June 26, 2026, extends the duo’s record of pairing club-focused EBM with anti-authoritarian themes.
items._cn_summary: 巴西电子二人组Aesthetische通过比利时独立厂牌Alfa Matrix发行数字EP《Every Beat Matters》，收录四首原创曲目及三首Chew The Loop的混音版本。音乐风格融合EBM、工业电子与舞曲，借鉴Front Line Assembly和Front 242的冰冷律动与机械节奏感，合成器钩子与有力的人声贯穿始终。这张EP以反极端主义为核心主题，封面文案明确反对威权言论、法西斯主义与战争，将每个节拍视为抵抗与团结的呼吁。该主题延续了二人组自2022年专辑《rvprty》以来对极右翼和反民主运动的批判立场。Gui Pires与Fab Viscardi自2012年组建项目以来，在Alfa Matrix厂牌下持续输出俱乐部导向的电子作品，将政治态度与音乐创作紧密结合。

items.body: Based in Barcelona, SDH (Semiotics Department Of Heteronyms) released their third album this year, marking their first release on Artoffact Records. The album offers ten relatively short tracks that blend a variety of influences. One moment, the music leans toward Electro-Wave; the next, it adopts a harder, Body Pop-inspired edge. Elsewhere, the sound shifts into more Pop-oriented territory, occasionally even embracing Dance elements. As a result, there is plenty to explore and discover throughout the record. Adding to its appeal is the distinctive half-whispered vocal style of Andrea Pérez, which gives the songs an intimate and recognizable character. Every track has something interesting to offer, although I personally find myself most drawn to the harder-hitting compositions. Diversity is undoubtedly the album’s greatest strength, making it accessible to a broad-minded audience with varied musical tastes. My only criticism is that some of the songs feel a little too short, leaving me wanting more. Nevertheless, this remains a highly enjoyable release, filled with memorable moments and several standout tracks. (Rating:8). Listen to “You Lost My Keys”: https://semioticsdepartmentofheteronyms.bandcamp.com/track/you-lost-my-keys
items._cn_summary: SDH来自巴塞罗那，这是他们在Artoffact厂牌发行的第三张专辑，收录十首短小曲目。整张专辑展现了丰富的风格跨度：时而偏向Electro-Wave的冷调合成器质地，时而融入Body Pop的硬朗节奏冲击，部分段落甚至加入更明确的流行旋律和舞曲元素。Andrea Pérez半低语的演唱方式为作品增添了私密感和辨识度，使每首曲目都带有统一的人声标签。专辑最大的优势在于多样性，能够同时吸引口味不同的听众；但部分曲目过于短促，未能充分展开。综合来看，这是一张在暗潮与合成器流行之间游走的作品，注重氛围营造与节奏感，融合度高但实验性有限。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — The guys are more settled on this their latest release, with Pete Mush (synths), Tom Tee (guitar), and Jaro (bass) now having a full-time drummer in Jazzper Coulier, who was one of three drummers on the 'Oneironauts'. Flautist Charles Sla is back again as a guest along with cellist Lyssa Toyimbo but no room this time for Ozric's Ed Wynne which is a shame, as if any band is continuing his work, it must be these Belgians. This is their tenth album, and the fifth I have heard out of the last six, and they are getting even more complex as they mix dance with space rock, psychedelia, tribal and so much more.When this album is on and the music is blasting out it is like nothing else exists as it takes control of the senses, and although they can slow it down when they wish and provide the contrast and dynamics which music needs to breathe, the listener knows it is just time to rest until they come back again with a vengeance. It is Ozrics mixed with Hawkwind with dashes of �resund Space Collective thrown in for good measure, but always direct and as much at home at a rave as it is between your ears when played on headphones (always at a decent volume). This is music beyond time and space, with guitars and synths knowing when to be mellow, but also when it is time to just let rip and go with the flow as they attack the senses. Yet another masterful instrumental collection from one of the top bands playing this style of expansive space/psychedelic rock.

items.body:
Mor Elian's first vinyl release on Fever AM since 2022, 'Built In Waves' is a taut set of dancefloor-ready house psychedelia that never overlooks the importance of bass.

Elian's got a reputation to uphold. Not only has she blessed her Fever Am label with some of its most memorable bangers - just check 'Double Dip' or its predecessor 'Diva Test' - but she moved into a different zone entirely last year when she released her debut album 'Solid Space', forming weightless ambient textures to hover between the frenetic rhythms. 'Built In Waves' is a comeback of sorts, then, that re-affirms her dedication to the dancefloor, with a selection of four techy, twitchy bangers that'll do the job whether you're in Berlin or Bogatá. 

The title track welds brain-tickling synths and Errorsmith-like vocaloid effects over skittering, syncopated percussion that Elian routinely interrupts with hand drums, constantly sculpting the low-end into a pulsing, momentous thud. And the cheeky 'Get Ready With Me' is even better, a jittery 'Spastik' tribute at first that Elian wakes up with rasping 'Flat Beat'-style bass before the EP concludes with the Panorama Bar-ready ass shaker 'Ondulations'.
items._cn_summary: 这是Mor Elian自2022年以来在Fever AM厂牌的首张黑胶发行，收录四首面向舞池的技术浩室作品。标题曲将挑逗感十足的合成器与近似Errorsmith的人声效果叠加在碎裂切分的打击乐之上，穿插手鼓打断节奏律动，低频被持续雕琢成脉动式的重击。'Get Ready With Me'以致敬Spastik的紧张抖动开场，随后用粗粝的低音线激活全曲能量，末曲'Ondulations'则是适合Panorama Bar清晨时段的律动型作品。乐评整体侧重功能性舞池描述，对声音设计层面的创新着墨有限。

items.body:
‘Aftersun’ composer Coates furnishes a score of heart-in-mouth classical strings, keys and choral arrangements to gay romance flick ‘Pillion’, aka an opportunity to ogle Alexander Skarsgård, replete with biker leathers, in a sub-dom relationship

By now one of the preeminent composers in his field - up there with Mica Levi, 0PN, Bobby Krlic et al - Coates continues to expand and hone his distinctly classic yet fresh palette and chops to purpose on this particularly lush set of orchestrations and sweeping sound design, including his take on a Satie evergreen. Gently gelled to the film’s narrative, revolving a shy yung queer lad seduced into a BDSM relationship with a dashing local biker, Coates’ score is ravishingly sensual and heady, full of oneiric allusions to classical, ambient, lavish ballads and twinkling electronica, all sure to hit pleasure centres of anyone who fancies Romance, Jonny Greenwood’s ‘Phantom Thread’ OST, Enya’s crushed velvet wafters, or event schmaltziest ends of Leyland Kirby.
items._genre: contemporary classical / orchestral / ambient / choral / electronica
items._cn_summary: Oliver Coates 为同性题材电影《Pillion》创作的配乐，延续了其在《Aftersun》中展现的当代古典语汇。全作以弦乐、键盘与人声合唱编排为核心，织体饱满且具有电影叙事所需的情感张力。作品中融入对萨蒂经典的重新诠释，兼具古典根基与新鲜质感，辅以梦幻氛围、缓拍电子声效和华丽弦乐铺陈，形成感官化的音乐叙事。整体风格游走于当代古典与氛围电子之间，情感表达偏向浪漫与感性，适合偏好细腻音色层次与电影配乐质感的听众。乐评将其与米卡·列维、Jonny Greenwood 等当代作曲家并列，肯定其在同类领域中的成熟度。

items.body:
One of the most distinctive and legendary vocal/dub albums of all time, recorded in 1981 by the “dub dentist” Keith Hudson, ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is now back in circulation for the first time in over 20 years, when it was first given overdue flowers via Basic Channel And Honest Jon’s ‘Basic Replay’ programme. It still burns with a rare energy, making it an untouchable, foundational text for the ages.

Keith Hudson (1946-1984) was one of dub reggae’s most distinctive innovators, renowned for a run of classic solo albums and productions for U-Roy, Big Youth, Ken Boothe and Horace Andy between 1972 and his untimely passing in 1984. However, Hudson's late period is where the real imperial juice can be found, a time that saw him move from Jamaican to London and New York studios, applying his unfathomable production style to a heavily americanised strain of vocal Soul. ‘Playing It Cool & Playing It Right’ is the pinnacle of that late period, an album that builds layer upon layer of alchemical brilliance.

Hudson’s combination of hooks and complex, highly unusual production is really unlike anything else from the period, or since, crooning in a soul mode made more haunting by a discreetly judicious application of tape FX, endlessly heavy subs, and mixing desk tricks deployed to delirious, almost psycho-acoustic effect.  The album was originally meant to feature one of Hudson's teenage sons to voice the dubs, but in the event the Love Joys, Wayne Jarrett, and inimitably Hudson himself featured at the microphone, with the dozen cuts co-produced by Wackies founder Lloyd ‘Bullwackie’ Barnes - the only collaboration between the two producers. It was originally issued on Hudson’s own label, Joint International, with subsequent pressings on Basic Replay in 2003, making it increasingly sought-after in the years since. 

Alongside reggae’s first concept album, ‘Flesh of My Skin, Blood of My Blood’, ‘Playing It Cool’ remains one the genre’s most important and unusual releases, picking up new disciples with every new wave of listeners taken aback by its stark, brooding blooze and brittle, spectral rendering.

items.body:
New Dream Machine 12" from Dutch producer Kennedy.

"Kennedy continues to sketch out imaginary worlds where thoughts and sensations are converted into sound via the power of machines. On this fifth instalment of Hi-Tech Soul, the Dutch producer channels fragments of midnight memories and daytime visions into something tactile yet elusive. As with previous chapters, the process remains shaped by surprise as hands and hardware entwine in a quiet, freeform dialogue.

The music itself drifts rather than drives, unfolding like shifting cloud forms that never quite settle. Loose, frayed house patterns hover in a state of flotation as basslines anchor just enough to stop everything dissolving completely. Each track has a sense of elevation where melodic synths filter through the mix like heavenly sunbeams breaking overhead. There's a constant progression to something that never comes, instead leaving you free to find your own meaning as textures blur into something soft, indistinct and gently euphoric.

A pure state of celestial suspension, 'Dream 5' is the newest offering in a series that takes you to a weightless world of infinite interpretations."

items.body:
After a few trips ‘Around the Sun’ Mr Fingers returns to the ‘floor with a definitively broad selection of deep house and acid aces betraying the sound’s links with soul jazz as much as Italo disco and ambient synth musics.

‘Leev Ur Mynd’ is the prescriptive title of Larry Heard’s 7th studio LP in his OG mode, which lands just over 40 years since his early 12”s initiated a sea-change in club music. On a dozen cuts the veteran effortlessly ushers debonaire dancefloors to his command, from proper ChItalo acid peacockery in ‘Plastic Nightmares’ to the piquant electro-soul flow of ‘Replicate’, and covering the finest spectrum of styles & patterns within a theme in between. 

His influential mastery of the 303 results in thee juiciest acid on the LP title tune, then tweaked to a charming type of bloozy jig in ‘Barndance’, and woven into the album’s tuffest jam ‘Menagerie’, or more subtly riding the piano-led glyde of ‘April Rain’, whereas the rest tends towards his equal bias for slicker soul-jazz and Afro-Latinate slink. Deeper lounge lizards will get theirs in the syncopated shimmy of ‘The Happening Thing’ and the sublime vocal chops of ‘When You Need Me’ and ‘All I Need’, thru the frankly sexy ‘Tension’ and that chef’s kiss twinkle of percussion and choral pads in ‘Ribbons.’

What a G?! Tip!
items._cn_summary: 这是Larry Heard以Mr Fingers名义发行的第七张录音室专辑，收录十二首作品，横跨近四十年俱乐部音乐经验。专辑标题为'Leev Ur Mynd'，延续早期十二寸单曲开创的风格脉络，将303酸性合成器线条与灵魂爵士、拉丁律动及Italo disco融合。曲目编排覆盖广泛风格光谱：'Plastic Nightmares'呈现意大利风酸曲姿态，'Replicate'展现电子灵魂律动，标题曲与'Barndance''Menagerie'凸显酸性合成器的多样运用，'April Rain'则以钢琴主导的滑行质感延伸抒情维度。'The Happening Thing'提供切分律动，'When You Need Me''All I Need'融入人声切片，'Tension'与'Ribbons'呈现打击乐与合唱垫音的细腻交织。作为资深制作人的成熟舞池宣言，作品在酸性电子与灵魂爵士的交叉地带展现出稳固的技艺与审美一致性。

items.body:
Strut Records presents a new reissue of the original Afrobeat classic Low Profile (Not For The Blacks), recorded and composed by Afrika 70 saxophonist and bandleader Lekan Animashaun and produced by Fela Kuti.

"After years touring the world as Fela’s baritone saxophonist, Animashaun stepped forward to lead the legendary Egypt 80 band following Tony Allen’s departure, remaining the group’s musical director until Fela’s death in 1997. He continued on subsequent tours with Seun Kuti until 2016.

Lekan began recording his only solo project, Low Profile, in 1977. The album was composed and recorded across sessions at home in Nigeria and on tour with Fela, who both produced the recordings and added keyboards to the album’s title track. ‘Low Profile (Not For The Blacks)’ referenced a government campaign during the country’s 1970s oil boom: “It was inspired by a speech by Olusegun Obasanjo, Nigeria’s military Head of State, when he urged black people to keep a low profile about their wealth and not to behave in a vulgar, arrogant way,” explains Lekan. “I argued that low profile is not just for the blacks, as everyone is human, regardless of race.” On the flip side, the simmering Afrobeat anthem ‘Se Rere’ (which translates as ‘Do Right’) delivers Animashaun’s message of living with integrity: do right, and you will reap what you sow. The song later became the band’s opening number during Fela’s live performances both in Nigeria and internationally throughout the 1980s and ’90s.

Despite recording beginning almost two decades earlier, Low Profile did not receive an official release until 1995, when it finally surfaced on Fela’s Kalakuta label. One of only a handful of albums led by core members of Kuti’s band, Low Profile captures a pivotal moment in Afrobeat history. Over time, the original has become a rare and highly sought-after record, and this new reissue places the spotlight back on a modest but influential Nigerian legend."
items._cn_summary: Strut Records 重新发行了尼日利亚萨克斯手 Lekan Animashaun 唯一的个人专辑《Low Profile》，原版由 Fela Kuti 制作并于 1995 年首次正式发行。专辑创作始于 1977 年，部分录制在尼日利亚本地，部分在 Fela 巡演途中完成。标题曲"Low Profile (Not For The Blacks)"回应了 1970 年代尼日利亚军政府首脑关于黑人在石油繁荣期应保持低调的言论，Animashaun 主张低调不分种族。B 面"Se Rere"（意为"做正确的事"）则成为 Fela 在八九十年代现场演出的开场曲，体现了以正直立身的非洲未来主义精神。专辑由 Afrika 70 乐队演奏，捕捉了 Afrobeat 发展史上的关键节点，将尼日利亚本土律动、Fela 式政治表达与爵士乐即兴融为一体。

items.body:
Bitchin' Bajas' Cooper Crain and Chicago mainstay Bill MacKay follow 2023's hazed 'Foreign Smokes' with another blunted blend of kosmische, West Coast new age, psychedelia and folk rock.

If you like Bitchin' Bajas, particularly their collaborations with Natural Information Society, there's a damn good chance that 'Stash' will hit you right in the third eye. We already know the Crain and MacKay are weathered players and we already know that their minds are in sync; 'Stash' picks up where its predecessor left off, providing a cinematic answer to the duo's obsession with classic American rock, German psych, vintage British folk, French exotica, Arab pop and Bollywood music. It's not subtle, but with just two basic instruments - Crain flips between organ and synth, while MacKay plays guitar - they don't have the need to pussyfoot. 'Stash' is never overworked, it's the result of two friends jamming out, plugging their instruments into a mixing desk and recording to 8-track to get the grit the material needs.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣圈资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首作品大多基于传统素材，融入手摇风琴、风笛、扬琴、长笛和弦乐等乐器，营造出古老而略带粗粝的氛围。开场曲《Svennedal》以奔跑般的节奏展示了主唱富有说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目《Nordgård》由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，加入手摇风琴与风笛形成推进力。扬琴为传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》提供细腻的声底，结尾曲《Orms》作为纯器乐作品，将手摇风琴、长笛与弦乐交织成失衡而奇特的声响。整体呈现出一种成熟的乐队气质，是对北欧传统声音的一次较为克制的探索，但实验性和跨界融合的程度有限。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统音乐作品，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥枪支暴力幸存者社区进行的实地田野录音。25位参与者年龄从17岁到67岁不等，在南区一栋老宅前廊录制了他们的真实声音，几乎未经过任何音乐加工，仅有少量即兴说唱穿插。录制当天恰逢特朗普下令向芝加哥部署国民警卫队，背景中隐约可闻机场航道与街头犬吠。一位失去两个儿子的年长女性在叙述中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，而编辑认为真正应该道歉的是社会本身。这张作品将田野录音、社群口述与即兴说唱融合为一种声音文献，旨在呈现芝加哥南区被遗忘角落的真实图景。所有收益将捐赠给反暴力公益组织。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自2013年马里音乐家Neba Solo（巴拉风琴）和Benego Diakité（恩戈尼琴）的原始录音，后由制作人Nick Gold与Ousmane Haïdara合作，将二重奏录音扩展为加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他与打击乐的合奏编制，并由三位女声伴唱补充。专辑以双CD形式发行，前半部分是经过重新编排的器乐与人声融合版本，后半部分应为原始二重奏录音。两种马里传统乐器——巴拉风琴与恩戈尼琴的搭配本身罕见，在此基础上叠加多层次声部与简约弦乐编配，展现了传统马里音乐在保持核心节奏与呼应式人声结构的同时向现代制作拓展的可能性。

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?
items.label: Ponderosa Music
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是意大利南部pizzica音乐五十周年的回顾之作。CanZoniere Grecanico Salentino乐队由Durantes家族创立，早期致力于复兴当地被遗忘的传统文化；现任主脑Mauro Durante接手后将这一声音推向全球。专辑重新编排了过去几十年的曲目，邀请原歌手与新一代乐手同台——老一辈歌手Rossella Pinto回归演唱代表作，新一代成员以合成贝斯等电子元素补充声场。Ludovico Einaudi的混音版《Taranta》也收录其中，展现了与当代古典钢琴家的跨界合作。整体上以原声乐器为主，保留了pizzica干燥、催眠的特质，同时通过新的编曲赋予作品当代色彩。这张作品既是对历史的致敬，也是跨代际的对话——扎根于本土传统，却面向未来。

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Filmed by Anja Riden, this session films Tissilawen at the foot of the Tassili n’Ajjer, the sandstone plateau over Djanet in the southeast of Algeria that handed them their name. The song they carried out there is “Kel Tamasheq,” the word the Tuareg keep for themselves, those who speak Tamasheq. The song first appeared on their 2012 debut Toumastin, an album whose name means “my origin.” Guitarists Bakrin Timlfati and Cheikh Taberni formed the band in 2008, childhood friends from Djanet who took Tinariwen as their model. “Kel Tamasheq” is their core desert blues: looping electric guitar over bass and hand percussion, with vocals in Tamasheq. Listen to “Kel Tamasheq” HERE and get your copy of Toumastin following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Tissilawen – Kel Tamasheq (outdoor session) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Well, this debut release came literally out of the wild blue yonder, an unexpected gift from my homeland, a sprawling 88-minute tour de force that just may go down as the 2026 Prog surprise of the year. What makes this particularly unique, the band is from my hometown of Miskolc, so this has a personal connection that I cannot and will not dismiss. As per norm in Magyar prog, the talented crew is led by keyboardist/guitarist Jozsef Simko, a tight rhythm section featuring bassist Tibor Kozak and Gergely Sumalan holding down the percussive elements rather perfectly. Add two more special members, a petulant and active Peter Toth on electric guitars and a French expatriate who decided to live in Hungary, Madeline Besson, who sings in perfect English, having been in a band called Molly Moonshine . The production and sound are pristine , the cover wholly attractive and the entire set of songs perched on a delicate balance between technical savvy by the players, and an overt feeling of humility that goes a long way to seduce the prog listener. I felt an immediate sense of maturity within the grooves, a comfort zone that embalmed my space all the way through the 'hidden door' that leads into my soul.The nearly 10-minute opener "Stray Heart" certainly prepares the journey behind the hidden door with an ultra shimmering flurry of electronic serenity, building up into a more petulant variation that had ulterior motives in mind, as both rock riffs and classical movements meld into a platform for introducing Madeline's silky warble, setting the tempo. The harder section seamlessly blend in without to many ruffles , shoveled ahead by basalt bass and demonic drumbeats, the guilty guitars unafraid to use just the right amount of effects, flowing into ambient pools of synthy bliss, before letting the singer emote in a hushed vein. Its pretty and magically soothing."Release" features some of finest violin work heard in ages (Nora Kacsenyak), with mournful cello (Vivien Netti Novak) aching along for the ride, the strings swirling infinitely as if caught in a gentle gale, the piano splendiferous, and a relief of tension that is palpable. It's an accessible prog piece that suggests a liberation that cannot be avoided. An obvious reference to a dearly departed relative (Jozsef's father), becoming quite the eulogy in this case. The gorgeous piano work emphasizes a moment of loving reflection that is worthy of both attention and praise.The mood becomes a tad grimmer on the brooding "Rachel Revisited", a song about domestic abuse from the female viewpoint, an ominous commentary on the weakness of spirit that has poisoned the human condition since the dawn of time. Madeline does a masterful job on the microphone, her crystalline voice appropriately fragile, at times even trembling like a swollen lip. The instrumental presentation is dark and low-key, with progressive accoutrements, scratchy effects and doomsday symphonics that veer towards pain, the splintered guitars quietly shrieking in the front row. Impressive powerful.For a country famous for its thermal waters, as it sits in a massive underground aquafer, and yet has no access whatsoever to any ocean or sea, "Coastline" can only refer to Lake Balaton or the Danube River. The spotlight is a delightfully intimate saxophone solo (Peter Czako) that should put wind to many a sail, a common site on the Hungarian Sea as the Balaton is often referred to. Yet the theme chooses to describe the vagaries of human relationships, the perpetual roller coaster ride of control and miscommunication, suddenly challenged by loving laughter and tender moments.Then, the stylistics take a huge turn into even more progressive exercises , we land on a trio of megalithic epics. Clocking in a colossal 27 minutes and change, "The Brother of Sleep" stamps the prog seal of classification without any hint of hesitation. The inspiration emanates from Oscar Wilde's "The Happy Prince", a rollicking storyline that injects slick percussion, tinges of harpsichord and an airy opening introduction, before eventually turning the rhythm section into on propulsion mode, the vocal gymnastics breathtaking as they lead and harmony voices intertwine. Another gear is put into motion as the echoing chorus becomes escorted by a sweeping organ motif drawing 'silver ribbons'. The third section has a harder drum pattern to rely on, a metallic shroud in the arrangement that underlines a restrained instrumental prowess that paints quite the canvas. The brazen bass is lovingly up-front and center in determining the shifting sonic transmission, settling into an explosive symphonic climax. Very cool opus."The Other Side" wishes to convey a sense of universality, reminding us of the benefits of respecting cultural identities, not surprising in lieu of the unicity of the Magyar ethnicity. The handclaps underline a communal environment as if sitting around a campfire, singing songs, sharing stories and playing music. Can there be a finer panacea, and a better embodiment of peace ? I think not and know of none better!This four-part suite evokes the Book of Revelation, the quarter of an hour epic "Riders" closes the curtain on the now open door, with a wondrous sonic adventure, where light and darkness somehow dare to co-exist. There is little doubt that here the progressive elements really gallop along nicely, like the valiant horses on the Puszta plain, imagining whips cracking the air, and Puli dogs doing their magical herding. Jozsef's elegant piano exudes a prototypical Magyar melancholia, a heady cocktail often mixed with a hint of stubbornness, playful pride and profound emotional commitment. The Peter Toth guitar solo is an ideal example, genuinely sorrowful at first and then building up into a taciturn frenzy without going deliberately crazy. The ambient piano mid-section is drop-dead beautiful, the solitude broken by a lone bass elevation that alters the pace into a bluesy organ-led adventure where Madeline gets to sing her thoughts. The upward staircase of sound rises inexorably to its mighty conclusion, with a grandiose final section, majestic and imperious , reaching for the heavens , a magnificent pinnacle that seals the deal.One of the finer debut heard in many a moon, what really stands out is the utter humbleness expressed throughout ,and in our increasingly turbulent noise factory society, this has been quite a soothing experience that should bear many future releases in the future. Highly recommended with or without a glass of palinka.4.5 fractured coils

items.body: Alfa Matrix has released Unter Null’s “The Rise From Ruin (and the Ritual of Becoming)” on June 26, 2026 as a limited double-CD digipak with an extended booklet, and as a download via Bandcamp. The set revisits the early Erica Dunham period of the project and is available now as a digital pre-order on Bandcamp and as a physical pre-order through the Alfa Matrix Store. At the centre of the release is “The Failure Epiphany”, the Alfa Matrix album that helped launch Unter Null’s early dark electro and industrial profile. The second disc expands that period with material from the EPs “Sick Fuck”, “Sacrament”, and “Absolution”, plus remixes by Noisuf-X vs. X-Fusion, Manufactura, T3chnophobia, Aslan Faction, Grendel, KiEw, Terrorfakt, and C-Drone-Defect. The release holds 34 tracks in total. The Rise From Ruin (and the Ritual of Becoming) (Deluxe Edition) by UNTER NULL About Unter Null Unter Null is the solo project of American musician Erica Dunham, founded in 1998 in Seattle, Washington. Initially rooted in power noise and harsh electronics, the project evolved into aggrotech/dark elektro through early self-released material and live dates in the early 2000s. Unter Null’s first full-length album, “The Failure Epiphany”, arrived in 2005 via Alfa Matrix (later re-issued with bonus material), following club traction around “Your Nightmare” and “Sick Fuck”. Touring in the U.S. and Europe followed in 2005–2006. On December 25, 2008, a house/studio fire destroyed Dunham’s recording equipment and jeopardized work then in progress. Despite the loss, files were recovered and Unter Null released “Moving On” in 2010 (Alfa Matrix), including expanded editions and international versions. Dunham later relocated for a period to Hamburg, Germany, before activity shifted again to the U.S. Pacific Northwest. The project continued sporadic releases and remixes through the 2010s. She also worked on her more atmospheric side project Stray in that period. In 2025, Unter Null returned with new studio material through Alfa Matrix, including the single “Coming Up To Breathe” (April 4, 2025) and the EP “You Made A Monster” (July 25, 2025). The EP features remixes by C-Lekktor, Leaether Strip, and Frontal Boundary and is distributed digitally via Bandcamp and other platforms. Unter Null also contributed remixes and collaborations in 2025, including featured work connected to Frontal Boundary.
items._cn_summary: Alfa Matrix厂牌于2026年6月发行Unter Null（Erica Dunham的个人计划）的双CD合辑，收录2005年专辑《The Failure Epiphany》及三张EP《Sick Fuck》《Sacrament》《Absolution》中的曲目，辅以Noisuf-X、Grendel、Terrorfakt等多位艺人混音，共34首。该计划1998年于西雅图创立，从早期的power noise和harsh electronics演变为aggrotech与dark elektro风格。2008年圣诞节的工作室火灾曾毁损录音设备，但2010年仍完成专辑《Moving On》。2025年通过《Coming Up To Breathe》单曲和《You Made A Monster》EP回归，C-Lektor、Leaether Strip等参与混音制作。该合辑以限量双碟digipak形式发行，附扩展册页，是对该项目早期阶段较为完整的回顾性整理。

items.body: LAHO, the Finnish dark electronic project of Konsta Vehkala, released the seven-track album “Death Machines” on June 26, 2026. The digital release gathers three of the project’s 2026 singles with four new tracks, among them a cover of Depeche Mode’s “Behind the Wheel”. LAHO blends industrial, EBM, futurepop and darkwave, with lyrics centred on dystopian themes and the darker side of human behaviour. Vehkala writes, programs and produces the project alone from Jyväskylä, Finland. “Death Machines” is the first LAHO album to feature vocals. Vehkala built the project’s earlier catalogue as instrumental work before resuming LAHO in 2024 after a 13-year break. The single “Programmed”, released on February 12, 2026, opened the new phase, followed by the singles “The Great Collapse” and “Last Rays of the Sun”. Death Machines by LAHO LAHO ‘Death Machines’ tracklist and the Depeche Mode cover “Death Machines” runs seven tracks: “Programmed”, “The Great Collapse”, “Cold New World”, “Decimated Memories”, “Fading Out”, “Last Rays of the Sun” and “Behind the Wheel”. The first, second and sixth tracks appeared earlier as standalone singles, while the other four are new to the album. The closing track reworks Depeche Mode’s “Behind the Wheel”, written by Martin L. Gore and first issued on the 1987 album “Music for the Masses”. Vehkala recorded, programmed and produced the album himself. He has tied the project’s lyrics to technology and modern life, describing the opening single “Programmed” as “a heavy hitting electronic track about our life in the ever-growing synthetic world.” The album is available digitally through Bandcamp. About LAHO LAHO is the solo project of Finnish musician and recording engineer Konsta Vehkala, based in Jyväskylä. It began in 2006 under the name Lahonnut Konkelo, a run of electronic and industrial experiments, with the name soon shortened to LAHO. The first EP, “The Other Side”, appeared in 2007 as a self-released CDr and was later reissued by the Italian netlabel Ekleipsi. Ekleipsi also issued the debut album “Escape from the Dying Star” in April 2009, a ten-track record made between 2007 and 2008 that mixed electro-industrial, synth work and distorted guitar. Vehkala followed it with the standalone track “The World in Flames” (2009), the single “Mechanigod” (2011) and the one-off digital release “Walking in the Air (1984 mix)” in December 2021. The project then went quiet for 13 years while Vehkala focused on other work. He resumed writing for LAHO in 2024 and added vocals as a permanent element, ending a previously instrumental catalogue. The 2026 singles “Programmed”, “The Great Collapse” and “Last Rays of the Sun” introduced the new direction. Alongside LAHO, Vehkala plays drums in the Finnish melodic metal band Psychework and has performed and recorded with Gian, Vipermilk and Lojohh, while contributing recording, mixing and mastering work to other Finnish acts. “Death Machines”, released on June 26, 2026, is the project’s first vocal-led album and its first full-length since 2009.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰单人项目LAHO由Konsta Vehkala独自完成创作、编程与制作，2026年6月发行七曲专辑《Death Machines》，收录三首单曲与四首新作，末尾翻唱Depeche Mode 1987年经典《Behind the Wheel》。这是LAHO首张加入人声的作品，此前其目录均为器乐作品。项目融合工业、EBM、未来流行与暗潮元素，歌词围绕反乌托邦与现代生活的阴暗面展开，开篇曲《Programmed》以沉重电子节拍探讨人造世界中的生存状态。芬兰于韦斯勒亚由独立音乐人独立发行，经Bandcamp数字平台发行，属小规模地下制作。整体以电子合成器为主体，结构偏向类型化，但融入人声后为此前纯器乐路线带来新的方向。

items.body: dreDDup, the industrial project from Novi Sad, Serbia, released a music video for the song “President Evil” on June 28, 2026. The dreDDup “President Evil” clip is the third single taken from the album “Pan/Dora” and, according to the band, the fourth dreDDup video made with AI technology, directed by founder Mihajlo Obrenov. The band brings a sound that mixes EBM, industrial and electronics, with distorted vocals and heavy programming; the band describes “President Evil” as an EBM/industrial track. Obrenov writes and produces the project from Novi Sad. Pan/Dora by dreDDup dreDDup’s ‘President Evil’ and the ‘Pan/Dora’ album “President Evil” is the tenth track on “Pan/Dora”, the band’s eleventh studio album, issued in 2024 and recorded at DURU Studio in Novi Sad. The band has framed the record as the start of a planned trilogy. Mihajlo Obrenov directed the video and built it with AI tools, continuing a run that began with the 2023 single “Clark Can’t“, the project’s first AI video, followed by “Cherry Noble” and “Not From Here“. The band states it plans two more videos for songs from “Pan/Dora” and is recording its next album. dreDDup also says it will mark 30 years of activity in 2027. About dreDDup dreDDup formed in 1997 in Novi Sad, Serbia, founded by Mihajlo Obrenov, who also records as miKKa, with drummer Robert Sabadoš. The project mixes industrial, EBM and electronics, and Obrenov has long described the sound as “demonic electronic”. Alongside the project, Obrenov runs the online label Crime:Scene Records, which he started in 2008, and the experimental project MRT, whose eleventh album “Kerrang” appeared in 2024. The band built a long catalogue across nearly three decades, reaching its eleventh studio album with “Pan/Dora” in 2024. From late 2023 the project paired new singles with AI-assisted videos, among them “Clark Can’t”, “Cherry Noble” and “Not From Here”. “President Evil”, released as a video on June 28, 2026, is the third single drawn from “Pan/Dora” and arrives as the band approaches its 30th year in 2027.
items._cn_summary: 塞尔维亚诺维萨德的工业计划 dreDDup 由 Mihajlo Obrenov 创立于1997年，长期以个人项目形式运作，近期为2024年第十一张录音室专辑《Pan/Dora》中的单曲《President Evil》发布了AI辅助制作的音乐视频。该项目自2023年起持续将单曲与AI生成的视觉结合，Obrenov负责所有创作与制作，鼓手 Robert Sabadoš 参与录制，声音融合EBM、工业和电子元素，失真人声配合重型编程，Obrenov将其风格自称为"demonic electronic"。除dreDDup外，他还运营在线厂牌Crime:Scene Records及实验计划MRT。2027年将迎来项目30周年。文章本身为新闻通稿性质，主要传递唱片信息与视频发布动态，未对音乐本体进行深入评论或审美分析，信息以事实陈述为主，缺乏对声音设计、创作手法或艺术价值的探讨。

items.body: Lucifers Bathroom, a dark alternative solo project from Germany, released the single “The Sigil” on June 15, 2026. The Lucifers Bathroom “The Sigil” single is the second to be drawn from the forthcoming debut EP “Red Wax”, following the first single “Shadows”. Lucifers Bathroom bring a dark alternative sound that mixes industrial, gothic and electronic elements, with distorted vocals and cinematic synth and guitar arpeggios. The project is the work of one artist, who has not been publicly named. Lucifers Bathroom’s ‘The Sigil’ and the ‘Red Wax’ EP “The Sigil” was mixed by Matthew Pansi. The track opens in near-silence over a distorted voice and minimal electronics, then builds through heavy drums, synths and guitar to a vocal that ends in a scream. The press material describes it: “Where debut single ‘Shadows’ sits with the darkness, ‘The Sigil’ breaks out of it. A track about liberation through fire — the burning need to break free from yourself, no matter how dark the world gets.” “The Sigil” follows “Shadows”, released on April 17, 2026. Both are singles from the debut EP “Red Wax”, which the project plans to issue later in 2026. The Sigil by Lucifers Bathroom About Lucifers Bathroom Lucifers Bathroom is a dark alternative solo project from Germany, launched in 2026. The music combines heavy electronic sound design, atmospheric textures and vocals, drawing on dark alternative, industrial and gothic influences. The artist behind the project has chosen to stay anonymous, and all tracks are written, produced and performed by one person. “Red Wax” is the debut EP. “Shadows” arrived as the first single on April 17, 2026, followed by “The Sigil” on June 15, 2026, with the EP set to follow later in the year.
items._cn_summary: Lucifers Bathroom是来自德国的暗潮单人项目，音乐融合工业、哥特与电子元素，作品以失真人声、电影感合成器与吉他分解和弦构建。"The Sigil"为其首张EP"Red Wax"的第二支单曲，编曲从近乎无声的失真人声与极简电子底色起始，逐步叠加重鼓、合成器与吉他，最终以呐喊式人声收束，呈现出从静态张力向爆发性释放的弧线。作品主题围绕以火焚毁旧我、从黑暗中挣脱的概念。整体制作由Matthew Pansi操刀混音，创作者保持匿名，所有创作与演奏均由一人完成。

items.body: Stars and the Underground, the New Zealand project of Auckland musician John Mason, released the single “Echolocation” on May 22, 2026. The Stars and the Underground “Echolocation” single features guest vocals from Hannah Berry of the Auckland dark-electronic project Talmar, and is the second single trailing the band’s forthcoming debut album “Guardians of the Night”. Stars and the Underground bring a sound that mixes post-punk, shoegaze and dark synth wave, with chiming guitars, low basslines and reverb-heavy vocals. John Mason handles vocals, guitars and bass, while John McDermott plays drums and produces. Echolocation by Stars and the Underground Stars and the Underground revisit ‘Echolocation’ with Talmar “Echolocation” is a reworked version of a song the band first issued on the limited “Evolution Circle EP” in 2019. For the 2026 single, the track was re-recorded with Hannah Berry of Talmar added on vocals. John McDermott recorded, mixed and mastered it at Arch Hill Studios in Auckland. The single follows “Lonely Black Hearts”, released on April 1, 2025, and both tracks point to the album “Guardians of the Night”. “While we have faced various challenges, I believe this has ultimately contributed to a stronger final product,” Mason stated. “‘Echolocation’ is a testament to this, as we initially introduced the concept in the limited release of the Evolution Circle EP. We chose to revisit the song, highlighting John McDermott’s exceptional drumming and production skills, along with Hannah’s enchanting contributions that elevate the track to new ethereal heights.” The video for “Echolocation” runs on the band’s official YouTube channel: About Stars and the Underground Stars and the Underground is a New Zealand project built around Auckland musician John Mason, who founded it in 2019. The current line-up pairs Mason on vocals, guitars and bass with John McDermott on drums and production; McDermott records the project at his Arch Hill Studios in Auckland. According to the band, Mason previously played in the New Zealand goth-rock group Winterland and McDermott in the Headless Chickens. The project debuted in 2019 with the “Evolution Circle EP”, which carried the first version of “Echolocation”. After a gap, the band returned on April 1, 2025 with the single “Lonely Black Hearts”, issued with remixes as the first single from the forthcoming debut album “Guardians of the Night”. “Echolocation”, released on May 22, 2026 with Hannah Berry of Talmar, is the second single drawn from that album. Talmar is the solo project of Auckland visual artist Hannah Berry, who makes dark electronic music.
items._cn_summary: Stars and the Underground 是来自新西兰奥克兰的音乐人 John Mason 主导的项目，2026年5月22日发行单曲《Echolocation》，由奥克兰暗电子项目 Talmar 的 Hannah Berry 担任客座人声。该曲是对2019年《Evolution Circle EP》中同名曲目的重新录制版本，由 John McDermott 在奥克兰 Arch Hill Studios 完成录音、混音和母带处理。音乐融合了 post-punk、shoegaze 和 dark synth wave 的元素，以清亮的吉他、沉稳的低音线和大量混响人声为特色。Mason 此前曾在新西兰哥特摇滚乐队 Winterland 任职，McDermott 则来自 Headless Chickens。《Echolocation》是即将发行的首张专辑《Guardians of the Night》的第二支单曲，紧随2025年4月的《Lonely Black Hearts》之后。Mason 表示重新录制这首歌曲旨在展现 McDermott 的鼓技与制作能力，以及 Hannah Berry 带来的空灵人声层次。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Andrew Chalk、Ralf Wehowsky与Eric Lanzillotta三位音乐人合作完成，分为两首长篇作品。A面在约克ICR录音室完成录音，由Colin Potter担任工程师；B面则在卡尔斯鲁厄创作。两首曲目分别以互补的标题呈现：Wycha与Chalawy暗示了材料在创作者之间的交换与回应。曲目延续了Chalk与Wehowsky长期合作的极简声响美学，以持续低音、缓慢演变的音色层和精密的混音技术为核心。整张专辑呈现的是一种去旋律化、去节奏感的静态聆听体验，蓝色彩胶限量首版548张，由Stoughton负责印刷，封面绘画出自Andrew Chalk本人。该作品收录于Anomalous Records这一专注于实验与即兴领域的小厂牌，与Cold Spring等冷系发行网络有所交集。原文仅为唱片信息汇编，缺乏实质性乐评内容。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张1993年由意大利厂牌发行的合作专辑，由意大利声音艺术家Giancarlo Toniutti与英国实验音乐人Andrew Chalk共同完成。两位艺术家分别在意大利乌迪内的室内与户外场地，以及英国约克郡ICR录音室（由Colin Potter担任工程师）采集素材。A面Tienalauami混合了1987至1988年间在两地录制的材料，B面Warkswood则以相反的录制顺序展开，两人各自在家中或录音棚完成混音。整张作品建立在田野录音与抽象电子手法的基础上，通过长时间的延展结构探索声学空间感。意大利与英国地下实验场景的跨地域合作，配合小厂牌出版与详尽的技术文档，体现了九十年代初欧洲实验音乐圈的独立美学取向。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了500位艺术家各自贡献的一段锁槽音轨（lock-groove），每一段都是一个无限循环的极简声响片段。由美国地下实验厂牌RRRecords于1998年发行，数量有限且编号发行。专辑形式本身就是一种概念艺术：将声音压缩到最短循环单元，让500种不同艺术家的声音美学在同一张黑胶上并置呈现。从极简嗡鸣到噪音碎片，从环境音到工业节奏，每段音轨都是一次微型实验。这种形式对实验音乐、噪音美学和前卫听觉探索有强烈兴趣的听众具有独特吸引力，但对于不熟悉此类极简概念的听众来说可能显得过于抽象。整体而言，它是一件实验性概念作品，聚焦声音本身的可能性而非传统音乐叙事。

items.body: Roots reggae singer Marcus Gad built his fifth album around the Kanak custom of his home island, New Caledonia, where communities share what the land provides. The title track “For All” puts that straight into its hook, changing a single word across one line: he chants “it a go shine for all” for the sun, then “it a go fall on all” for the rain. The sun and the rain reach everyone, and nobody owns either. The singe marks the first time Gad unites his distinct recording frameworks, combining the organic instrumentation of his live band Tribe with the electronic engineering of producer Tamal. Tribe lays down a slow, steady one-drop riddim guided by Franck Paulin‘s organ work and a full brass section, while Tamal handles the final mix and digital layers. Out on 19 June through Easy Star Records and Big Scoop Records,, For All is Gad’s first album in three years. items._cn_summary: 新喀里多尼亚歌手Marcus Gad的第五张专辑以故乡卡纳克传统中'土地共享'的观念为核心，标题曲通过一句歌词的单词变化表达阳光与雨水属于所有人的理念。制作上首次将现场乐队Tribe的有机编制与制作人Tamal的电子混音结合，弗兰克·保兰的风琴与完整铜管声部支撑起稳定的one-drop雷鬼节奏骨架，再叠加数字化的混音层次。这张作品由Easy Star Records与Big Scoop Records联合发行，是Gad三年来的首张专辑，呈现出根植于传统雷鬼但融入大洋洲原住民文化视角的跨界特质。

items.body:
Back by demand - 2nd hand copies are known to trade for triple figures - Cindy’s timeless suite of sexy, hazed dream-pop is acutely tipped to anyone who holds a flame for Julee Cruise, Voice Actor, Lynch, Enya, Bianca Scout, Vince Clarke...

‘I’m Cindy’ is a chef’s kiss of effortlessly slow, seductive lo-fi songwriting that practically smushes earlobes with its heavenly marriage of Kai Hugo's faded production lustre and singer, Blue LoLãn’s range of whispered sweet nothings and harmonised coos. In the years since its original release it’s taken on a life of its own as a go-to succour for lovers of blissed-out, cinematic waft with equal measures of soft-focus, nostalgic FM synths and details that caress and crack in all the right, tender places. 

Conceptually derived from Palmbomen II’s ‘Memories of Cindy’ session of 2017, the 13 tracks find marbled whorls of sensual fascination within that LP’s fantasy reminiscence, here expanded into a spectrum of LA-via-Antwerp dream-pop like Johnny Jewel meets Alex Zhang Hungtai on the synth and sax pearl ‘Another’ or lip-smacking cruiser ‘Justin’, thru a Voice Actor-esque ‘Voice Message’ and the gossamer FM synth fronds that wrap it up on ‘Maybe Because It’s Over Now’, whilst secreting shimmers of Vince Clarke ballads in ‘2y & 6m’, and acid-laced lo-fi machine crack shades away from Maria Minerva on ’Never Let Me Go’.

No brainer!
items._cn_summary: Cindy的《I'm Cindy》是一张以梦幻流行（dream-pop）为底色的全长专辑，呈现出慵懒、朦胧且具有电影感的质感。制作人Kai Hugo以低保真手法处理合成器与人声，歌手Blue LoLãn以低语式演唱与和声铺陈贯穿全作，营造出柔软而带怀旧感的声场。专辑概念源自Palmbomen II 2017年的'Memories of Cindy'录音，十三首曲目在此基础上扩展，融合了Lynch式的氛围叙事、Vince Clarke式的合成器旋律脉络，以及Maria Minerva式的低保真酸性电子碎片。从比利时的独立厂牌发行，整体偏向私密化的卧室流行审美，强调氛围与情绪的绵延，而非结构上的实验性突破。

items.body:
Surf Gang co-founder Eera comes correct on his first solo album, trading brittle cloud rap for squashed trance and tempered EDM and connecting with Mechatok, Nick León and CRUSH3d in the process.

If you didn't know by now, Surf Gang aren't your average rap production outfit. Evilgiane is regularly seen on underground festival bills, playing back-to-back with Evian Christ or palling around with Skrillex, while Harrison decided to go the atmospheric route on his solo debut 'Taking a walk & calling a car home', following his production on 'POMPEII // UTILITY' with a sequence of moody instrumentals. Cameron Kozloff, better known as Eera, takes a different route entirely, following the undercurrent of blown-out, saccharine dance music that's flourishing on YouTube, TikTok and Bandcamp if you're prepared to look beyond the anime artwork and videogame references.

Really, what Eera's isolated is that rap and contemporary trance have plenty in common - Araabmusik wasn't heading down a creative dead end when he released 'Electronic Dream' all those years ago. And 'Just Keep Holding On' sounds impressively plugged in; it's packed out with zeitgeist-y themes that might as well have been snatched from a PS2-era RPG (just check 'I Know' and prepare to weep) and features some unexpected guest appearances. León assists on 'Just Being Honest', a romantic, whimsical track that mutates into Daft Punk-like electro house and Berlin's Mechatok mucks in for lead single 'Sad But So Funny', a Robert Miles-alike piano-led banger.
items._genre: electronic / trance / cloud rap / EDM / electro house
items._cn_summary: Surf Gang 成员 Eera 的首张个人专辑脱离了原本脆裂的云说唱路线，转向挤压式 trance 与节制化的 EDM 制作。专辑核心立论在于说唱与当代 trance 共享结构逻辑，因此大量情绪化合成器编排与扭曲的低保真处理取代了原本的人声节奏。与 Mechatok 的合作单曲融入 Robert Miles 式的钢琴旋律，Nick León 参与的曲目则在浪漫氛围中滑向 Daft Punk 风格的 electro house。整体声音美学借鉴了 PS2 时代 RPG 的配乐气质，视觉上偏向 YouTube 与 Bandcamp 上流行的动漫与电子游戏文化圈层，是一张从地下说唱制作转向电子舞曲领域的跨界尝试。

items.body:
Following 2024's avant-prog-Americana song cycle 'Viewfinder', guitar deity Wendy Eisenberg goes chamber pop on their self-titled latest, tipping their hat to Judee Sill, Gillian Welch, Van Dyke Parks and Joanna Newsom.

When they relocated from rural Western Mass to Brooklyn in 2020, Eisenberg was hit with a wave of longing for the open landscape they'd left behind. They were drawn to classic country and folk records, perfectly poised offerings from Willie Nelson and John Hartford and lavish pop-folk records from Jimmy Webb and Van Dyke Parks as well as the weirdo fare of Richard Dawson et al. So when 'Viewfinder', a way of deconstructing the experience following eye surgery in 2011, was finished, Eisenberg started writing "genuinely folk songs" and swapping out their usually showy, complex performance for a form of relative simplicity that they explain is inherently strange all the same. Prog becomes folk, basically. And they're not on their own; more eaze handles the lush string arrangements, playing pedal steel and synthesizer, and a loose band forms around that axis, with drummer Ryan Sawyer and bassist Trevor Dunn.

But despite the personnel, it's resolutely Eisenberg's album. Their voice sounds unrestrained, capturing the era they're referencing and their own emotional (and physical upheaval). It's fragile but strangely warm on the country-tinged Jim O'Rourke-like 'Will You Dare' and hypnotic on the baroque 'Meaning Business', a track they wrote in the wake of David Lynch's death as the antithesis of the "Lynchian" aesthetic. And they should really get their flowers for this one; Americana, especially now, is teetering on a precipice, almost knocked off the edge by half-assed, churned attempts and underwritten pastiches. Eisenberg's an attentive listener and someone who's surrounded themself with similarly sensitive ears, people who are able to fill their heart and their sound so what we hear is as byzantine as a Gastr del Sol record but sounds as effortless as John Prine's 'Angel From Montgomery'. If you loved Joanna Newsom's 'Ys' and have never found anything quite as satisfying, this is the one.
